articles.title: El emotivo mensaje de Ilia Topuria a su hermano Aleksandre antes de su pelea
articles.standfirst: El mayor de los Topuria se enfrenta mañana a Santiago Luna en UFC Qatar
articles.summary: El mayor de los Topuria se enfrenta mañana a Santiago Luna en UFC Qatar
articles.body: Mañana es el día. Este sábado, Aleksandre Topuria (7-1) subirá a la jaula de UFC Qatar para buscar su tercer triunfo en UFC. Esta vez, ante el mexicano Santiago Luna (8-1). Y a su lado, en su esquina, estará su hermano Ilia Topuria. El doble campeón de la UFC, un año menor que Aleksandre, 'reaparece' en un acto de UFC desde que ambos, con los papeles intercambiados, abandonaron derrotados el jardín sur de la Casa Blanca. Por aquel entonces, fue el hombro de Aleksandre el que sostuvo a Ilia Topuria. Ahora es el 'Matador' el que actúa como apoyo para 'El Conquistador' en su ascenso hacia el título del peso gallo. Y en la previa, Ilia dedicó un emotivo texto en redes sociales a su hermano 'Sandro': "Hermano mío, quiero felicitarte por todo el trabajo, el sacrificio y la entrega que te han traído hasta aquí. Nadie en este mundo conoce mejor que nosotros el camino que hemos recorrido. Nadie sabe realmente lo que nos ha costado llegar hasta aquí, las dificultades que hemos superado, las veces que hemos tenido que levantarnos y todo lo que hemos dejado atrás para perseguir nuestros sueños. Todo empezó con dos hermanos que soñaban con tener una bicicleta para compartir. Y hoy, uno de esos niños se ha convertido en una inspiración para millones de personas. Pero lo que más me llena de orgullo no es lo que has conseguido, sino la persona en la que te has convertido. Porque yo sé quién eres, de dónde vienes y el corazón que hay detrás de cada batalla. Mañana no subes solo a ese octágono. Contigo suben nuestros sueños de niños, nuestros sacrificios, nuestra historia y todos los que nunca dejaron de creer en nosotros. Mañana la victoria te pertenece, porque te la has ganado con sangre, sudor y fuego. Pase lo que pase, para mí siempre serás un campeón, mi hermano mayor y uno de los mayores orgullos de mi vida. Te quiero con toda mi alma, hermano. Que Dios te acompañe mañana y siempre".

articles.title: Lauren Price beats Kotaskova to become undisputed world welterweight champion
articles.summary: Lauren Price dominates Michaela Kotaskova to seal her place in history by becoming undisputed world welterweight champion.
articles.body:
Lauren Price dominated Michaela Kotaskova to seal her place in history by becoming undisputed world welterweight champion.

Price, 32, took an unanimous, shut-out decision and the acclaim of the crowd to add the WBO title to her collection and become the first Welsh fighter to claim the accolade of holding all four major world titles.

Already an Olympic champion and world champion from her amateur days, it further underlined her claim as being among the very best in boxing.

But the way in which she did it, extending a perfect professional record to 11 wins from her 11 fights, suggested there could yet be more to come.

Price v Kotaskova: Watch undisputed title fight after Edwards v McGregor

History, hunger and headline bills - why Price is box office

Edwards' world title aim to join Welsh boxing greats

Price won every round from every judge in front of a partisan Cardiff crowd, producing an unrelenting pace that punished her opponent at every opportunity.

Although Price could not force a stoppage, there was never any doubt she had done enough against an opponent full of stamina and stubbornness.

Kotaskova, beaten only once, but never stopped in her career, showed real heart but had no answer to Price's expertise.

The Tokyo gold medal winner could celebrate even before the final bell sounded, climbing the corner ropes and into the record books.

It was lapped up by a sell-out Utilita Arena crowd who excitedly acknowledged the achievement and the moment.

Wales has produced 14 world champions, some of them genuine greats.

They include, of course, Joe Calzaghe who so often graced this venue with successful defence after successful defence of his super-middleweight crown.

He never reached undisputed status, though he was able to cross the capital city to go from arena to stadium champion.

That is the next challenge for Price, claiming before she left the ring that more is to come while talk immediately turned to five-weight world champion Claressa Shields as a stadium fight next summer.

That is for the future, but this was a night for history - with the calibre of some of the former boxers in the stands a nod to that.

Champions know champions. Five Welsh world title winners were in the capital to watch their compatriot do something never been done before.

From Cinderella Man Steve Robinson and Barry Jones, to the more recent Joe Cordina, who may still be eyeing a stadium return of his own in the coming weeks.

All have been proud to fly the flag, but perhaps none have worn it quite as much on their sleeve - or shorts - as Price has done.

Here, entering to the strains of a Welsh male voice choir, the atmosphere moved from Friday night in a city centre to full-blooded patriotism.

The anthem stirred so much Kotaskova couldn't help but raise an eyebrow before stepping out of her corner.

From then, she had no time to savour the moment let alone consider become an opportunity the Czech Republic's first world champion.

She felt flurries of punches from the first moments and struggled with the unrelenting pace set by the champion.

Steely-eyed, Price refused to allow a breath and, while Kotaskova continued to try and come onto the front foot, she was met by angry, but calculated attacks.

Kotaskova's problems only increased when she was cut in the fifth round, the hooks from the home fighter providing no let up.

At one point in the seventh, Kotaskova took a shot so fierce she almost turned her back to say no more, but still she came and still Price went hunting with hooks.

She could not find the decisive blow, finally letting the tempo slip, and even enjoying the final seconds as she accepted she had done more than enough to win and win a place in boxing history.

Edwards impresses in significant undercard win

Price was not the only Welsh winner on the night as Rhys Edwards secured a significant victory over Lee McGregor, taking an unanimous decision to claim the WBA Continental featherweight championship.

McGregor, 29, had stepped back down to featherweight after two defeats in his last three bouts and had made it clear he knew his chances of returning to world-challenging level was on the line.

His determination to keep coming forward showed what it meant, soaking up several clean shots, but Edwards proved too quick and too sharp.

The 26-year-old from Penygraig also had something to prove after a disappointing draw with Gully Powar last time out.

Then he faded in the latter round, but here Edwards managed to take McGregor's punches and maintain his own pace. It ensured what is perhaps the biggest win of his career, and to leave McGregor contemplating his options.

Elsewhere on the undercard, Willy Gilheaney's unbeaten record was taken away by the experience of Argentinean Alberto Igancio Palmetta, the former Olympic boxer showing plenty of know-how to overcome the Swansea fighter's guts and early control to take an unanimous points win.

Earlier in the night, Doncaster's Jake Goodwin took the decision in a game middleweight bout with Liverpool fighter Sean Arkwright. Goodwin – who had former world featherweight champion Josh Warrington in his corner – had only accepted the fight on two weeks' notice, accepting before he was even granted time off work.

And there were wins for Welsh fighters Brandon Scott and Kane Shepherd, while Cardigan's Josh Mellor and Newport's Lewis Howells fought to a draw.

articles.title: Machine Gun Shooting Mitchell Details Wild Hangout With Strickland
articles.summary: Bryce Mitchell has proven to be one of the wildest and most outspoken fighters on the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) roster, but even “Thug Nasty” had...
articles.body:
Bryce Mitchell has proven to be one of the wildest and most outspoken fighters on the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) roster, but even "Thug Nasty" had a tough time keeping up with UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland during a recent hangout.

It's no secret that Mitchell and Strickland are two of the biggest UFC problem children. They say anything that is on their minds and it's usually controversial or derogatory to a specific group of people. UFC has continued to give both fighters a platform to speak and perform, which has given Mitchell and Strickland years to create drama. Strickland more so than Mitchell due to his championship tenure.

With all of that in mind, fight fans were intrigued to see how the two fighters would get along during a recent hangout. Mitchell visited Strickland in Las Vegas for a day of excitement, which included gun shooting, mixed martial arts (MMA) training, dirt bike riding, and basketball. Mitchell ended up having the "time of my life."

Check it out below and let us know if this is your idea of a day of fun!

"I had the time of my life," explained Mitchell during a recent Instagram post . "For the first time in my life I rode a dirt bike. I rode one a couple times, but not like I did yesterday.

"Fluffy was there, too. Fluffy coached me a lot. I was actually on Fluffy's bike and then we shot machine guns. Never shot a machine gun.

"It was awesome. I'm actually a pretty good shot with it. You just got to really hold that one down and hold that trigger and commit to it.

"And we also played a game of basketball. It was blacks versus whites. It was so fun though man.

articles.title: Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev prediction, pick, start time, odds for UFC Qatar
articles.summary: Exciting flyweights Asu Almabayev and Kyoji Horiguchi could be in for a Fight of the Night in Qatar.
articles.body:
Kyoji Horiguchi and Asu Almabayev meet on the UFC Fight Night 294 main card at ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar. Check out this quick breakdown of the matchup from MMA Junkie analyst Dan Tom.

Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev UFC Fight Night 294 preview

Horiguchi (36-6 MMA, 9-2 UFC) aims to rebound from the first loss of his second UFC stint. After defeating Tagir Ulanbekov and Amir Albazi, Horiguchi lost a key matchup against Manel Kape in June.

Almabayev (24-3 MMA, 7-1 UFC) will look to make it four in a row. His current winning streak includes wins over Jose Ochoa, Alex Perez and Charles Johnson.

Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev UFC Fight Night 294 expert pick, prediction

Filling out the main card is a men's flyweight attraction between ranked fighters, Kyoji Horiguchi and Asu Almabayev.

I'm happy to see this division being featured more prominently in 2026, and both Horiguchi and Almabayev are fighters deserving of the attention.

Almabayev has continued to make steady improvements off of his lone setback in the octagon, but I suspect that powerful strikers who can counter grapple still provide problems for the Kazakh fighter.

Horiguchi's defense is not beyond reproach, but the former UFC title challenger has made serious strides in his wrestling since moving shop to American Top Team and brings a wealth of experience into this matchup.

I expect a tight and tedious affair to score considering the styles and output at play, but I'll pick Horiguchi to edge out a decision win by landing the more meaningful and impactful offense.

Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev UFC Fight Night 294 odds

The oddsmakers and the public favor the Japanese fighter, listing Horiguchi -188 and Almabayev +152 via FanDuel.

Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev UFC Fight Night 294 start time, how to watch

Horiguchi and Almabayev are expected to walk to the cage at approximately 12:40 p.m. ET. The fight streams live on Paramount+ .

articles.title: El gran día de Aleksandre Topuria
articles.standfirst: 'El Conquistador' pelea esta tarde en Qatar (18.30h) ante el mexicano Santiago Luna
articles.summary: 'El Conquistador' pelea esta tarde en Qatar (18.30h) ante el mexicano Santiago Luna
articles.body: Un año después, Aleksandre Topuria (7-1) regresa al último octágono que pisó como peleador: el del Ali Bin Hamad al-Attiyah Arena, en Doha, Qatar. Allí, hace exactamente un año, venció a Almakhan en su segundo combate en la UFC. Ahora busca el pleno con su tercer triunfo en la mejor liga de MMA del mundo. Para ello, tendrá que superar este sábado (18.30 horas, aproximadamente, en Eurosport y HBO Max), al mexicano Santiago Luna (8-1). Será un choque de estilos precioso para cerrar la cartelera preliminar en un combate en el que el ganador quedará a las puertas del top-15 del peso gallo. Aleksandre Topuria, como demostró ante Thicknesse y Almakhan, es un peleador muy completo al que únicamente se le puede echar en cara no haber finalizado a ninguno de sus rivales. Pero el control y el dominio sobre ellos fue casi abosluto. Tras una larga inactividad derivada de su entrega como entrenador a la carrera de Ilia, posiblemente pelear dos combates completos era lo mejor que podía pasarle. "Tengo mi propia historia", explicaba en MARCA esta semana, lamentando no haber podido pelear más este año... cuando su objetivo era hacer, al menos, dos combates, como en 2025. Pero el objetivo no cambia: seguir escalando. "Es un rival más que lo tengo por delante y lo tengo que pasar por encima. Punto y final", desarrollaba. “La pelea verdadera es fuera del octágono. Al final, dentro son 15 o 25 minutos máximos. La pelea dónde tienes que mostrar lo que vales es realmente fuera. La pelea verdadera es la vida”, reflexionaba ‘El Conquistador’ horas antes de dar el peso, este viernes. Tanto él como Luna clavaron las 136 libras del peso gallo, oficializando el duelo de un evento que comandará el Prochazka vs Stirling y donde, por ejemplo, también estará el prometedor peleador argentino Kevin Vallejos. El hispanogeorgiano mantiene su filosofía: confía en sus posibilidades y sabe el trabajo que ha hecho durante todo el campamento. Y las apuestas, de forma clara además, están con él: es muy favorito. Luna, mientras, es un gran prospecto: viene de perder ante Bryce Mitchell (que fue arrasado en el pasado por Ilia Topuria), pero su inició fulgurante en la UFC no se ha apagado. Es un buen ‘wrestler’ (no al nivel de Aleksandre) y como todo peleador mexicano, peligroso en el boxeo. Una gran prueba para medir el nivel de Aleksandre.

articles.title: WOW 34 Valencia, un regreso histórico al Roig Arena
articles.standfirst: La compañía líder de MMA en España vuelve hoy al lugar donde batió todos los records el pasado sábado
articles.summary: La compañía líder de MMA en España vuelve hoy al lugar donde batió todos los records el pasado sábado
articles.body: Esta tarde, el Roig Arena volverá a vestirse de gala para albergar WOW 34 Valencia, un evento histórico en el que se llevarán a cabo varios combates de vital importancia para la compañía. En este mismo escenario, WOW FC batió el récord de asistencia a un evento de MMA en España el pasado abril, reuniendo a 14.000 espectadores en una velada para el recuerdo. En este ocasión se espera algo similar para que la compañía y las MMA en España sigan creciendo de manera exponencial como han hecho durante todo el año. En el combate estelar, Luis Iván Rodríguez (11-2) se medirá a Felipe Dos Santos (11-3) en un duelo que posiblemente decida al siguiente contendiente al título vacante de peso mosca. Tras la marcha de Fabià Sintes a la UFC no hay un campeón establecido en la división, y el peleador mexicano viene de superar notablemente a todo un mítico de la promotora como Davi Santos. Además, el peleador brasileño también busca volver a la UFC después de medirse a nombres de la talla de Lone'er Kavanagh, Manel Kape o André Lima. La pelea co estelar será la más emotiva de todas, ya que será el combate de retirada de Enrique 'Wasabi' Marín (14-8) ante César 'Goku' Arzamendia (9-7). El peleador español ha sido pionero en España en las MMA y es toda una leyenda, por lo que no hay mejor sitio en el que decir adiós que en un Roig Arena lleno hasta la bandera para despedir a una de las personas que ha permitido que las artes marciales mixtas evolucionen tanto en nuestro país. El evento también contará con otros grandes duelos, como el de Mor Dieye (5-0) ante Timur Kurbankadiev (6-1). El compañero de gimnasio de Joel Álvarez continúa invicto y ya venció a Nico Medina en el Roig Arena hace unos meses, por lo que buscará prolongar su récord invicto en busca de ganarse la pelea titular de una vez por todas. Además, otro que también estuvo presente en Valencia hace unos meses fue David Hervías (3-0), que en esta ocasión se enfrentará a Luis Hernández (6-1) para volver a demostrar por qué es uno de los mayores diamantes en bruto de las MMA españolas. En su debut en WOW FC David sufrió de lo lindo, y en esta ocasión volverá a tener un reto mayúsculo que le permita subir al siguiente escalón dentro de la compañía. Más allá de estos enfrentamientos, la cartelera también contará con otros grandes duelos como el de Dimitri Barkaia (1-0) vs Michele Balducci (1-1), el debut profesional de Mouslim Saidoulaev (0-0) ante Adonis Montero (0-1) o el combate entre Klim Gusyev (2-0) y Tome Bokofo (1-1), candidato a llevarse el bono de la noche. Otra velada que se espera que sea histórica y que se recordará durante mucho tiempo.

articles.title: Lauren Price set for Cardiff stadium fight after unifying welterweight division
articles.summary: Lauren Price is one of the most decorated fighters in British boxing history and is now set to headline a summer stadium show in Cardiff.
articles.body:
She is already one of the most decorated fighters in British boxing history, and now Wales' Lauren Price is set to headline a summer stadium show at Cardiff City Stadium or Cardiff Arms Park.

Price dominated Michaela Kotaskova in Cardiff on Friday night, winning every minute of every round as she became Wales' first unified boxing champion by locking up the welterweight division.

With her stack of titles added to an Olympic gold medal , Price is now set to get to the next level, with negotiations already progressing for a stadium contest in the summer, with Chantelle Cameron or Mikaela Mayer – who fight on Christmas Eve – among the list of possible opponents.

Price beats Kotaskova to become undisputed champion

Price becomes Wales' first undisputed champion - as it happened

The 32-year old Welsh fighter was so dominant in unifying the division on Friday it prompted her usually reserved trainer, Rob McCracken, to name her as the world's best female fighter, and now Price is set for a bumper 2027.

"If we can bring the big names and the big fights to a stadium, it's going to make a massive difference to Wales and Cardiff and everyone involved, and Lauren is very passionate about that," Price's promoter Ben Shalom told BBC Sport Wales.

"She is unique in the attention that she can generate and therefore I think she can demand to make sure that the fights happen in Wales.

"A lot of eyes will be on [Chantelle] Cameron and [Mikaela] Mayer's fight, and that is a fight [the winner versus Price] that we'd love to make.

"That fight in May or June at Cardiff Rugby Club or Cardiff City Football Club, you know, you're doing 15-20,000 ticket sales with Lauren Price there, so fingers crossed."

BBC boxing expert Steve Bunce says a deal for a stadium fight in the summer has been agreed, with a mandatory defence likely to come first in February. France's Emilie Sonvico has been touted as a possible opponent.

"She has a sneaky fight in February and then an outdoor fight in May or June, at Cardiff City Stadium, that's done and dusted, that's going to happen," he told BBC Sport.

"It won't be Claressa Shields in the opposite corner, but it will be a big opponent in May or June outdoors in the Welsh sunshine."

Price feels she needs to move to bigger capacity venues to secure her legacy, despite already being one of the most decorated fighters in British boxing history.

"It's about now moving on to what's next, and there is talks that it could potentially be a stadium fight in the summer, and that's what it's about now, the legacy and the fan base growing," she explained.

Price's trainer McCracken, who runs the Team GB boxing programme, says the Ystrad Mynach southpaw is now the best female fighter on the planet and only likely to improve.

"Lauren's been an incredible female boxer for Great Britain; she's won the Olympics, she's won the World Championships, European Games, everything, every belt in boxing at welterweight," he told BBC Sport Wales.

"She is only going to do more and improve and gain from this experience; there's a massive journey still to come. She's only had 11 professional fights.

"She's done her bit, learned, developed and gained the experience… and I feel she's the best female in the world.

"I have done for about 18 months, and I think she'll only improve and she'll only get better.

"In my lifetime, Joe Calzaghe is probably the best British professional I've ever seen, and I feel Lauren Price is the best female that I've ever seen. She's a super talent.

"There are bigger nights in Wales for Lauren and for everybody, and it will be a fantastic journey to be a part of."

articles.title: UFC Fight Night: Prochazka vs. Stirling Live Updates, Highlights and Results
articles.summary: The UFC is back in Qatar today, which means a nice early start for fight fans in North America.
articles.body:
The UFC is back in Qatar today, which means a nice early start for fight fans in North America.

Headlining honors for the card will go to a high-stakes light heavyweight clash, with former champ Jiri Prochazka taking on surging contender Navajo Stirling. Prochazka will be looking to rebound from a disastrous loss to Carlos Ulberg in a failed bid for the vacant light heavyweight belt. Stirling, who is fresh off a knockout win over Jan Blachowicz, will attempt to lock up his own shot at the title, though the fact that he trains with Ulberg could make things complicated.

The co-main event will also have definite title stakes, as former bantamweight champ Aljamain Sterling takes on Kevin Vallejos at featherweight. Sterling is riding a win over Youssef Zalal and Vallejos recently took out Josh Emmett. Another big win for either man in Qatar could set up a showdown with legendary champ Alexander Volkanovski.

There's plenty more to look forward to on today's lineup too. Earlier on the card, Brian Ortega will make his lightweight debut against the always entertaining Dan Hooker. Fan favorite flyweight Kyoji Horiguchi will also return to action, taking on fellow contender Asu Almabayev.

The undercard will begin at 10:00am ET, and the main card will kick off at at 1:00.

Keep it locked here for live results of all the action in Qatar.

UFC Fight Night: Prochazka vs. Stirling Full Card

Light Heavyweight: Jiri Prochazka vs. Navajo Stirling

Featherweight: Kevin Vallejos def. Aljamain Sterling by unanimous decision (30-27, 29-28, 30-27)

Lightweight: Dan Hooker def. Brian Ortega by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

Flyweight: Kyoji Horiguchi def. Asu Almabayev by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

Middleweight: Ikram Aliskerov def. Jared Cannonier by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

Bantamweight: Santiago Luna def. Aleksandre Topuria by split decision (29-28, 30-27, 28-29)

Heavyweight: Tallison Teixeira def. Shamiel Gaziev by unanimous decision 29-28, 29-28, 30-27

Flyweight: Amir Albazi def. Alessandro Costa by submission (rear-naked choke) at 4:34 of round 3

Catchweight (172 lb): Tahir Abdullayev def. Jake Matthews by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

Lightweight: Dom Mar Fan def. Nikolas Motta by unanimous decision (30-26, 30-26, 29-27)

Light Heavyweight: Diyar Nurgozhay def. Alik Lorenz by TKO (head kick and punches) at 0:24 of round 2

Lightweight: John Mitchell def. Shoaib Yousaf by TKO (knee and punches) at 3:50 of round 1

Despite their shared knockout power, Jiri Prochazka and Navajo Stirling both made it through round one. It was a tough one to score, as the two light heavyweights spent most of five minutes attempting to get a good read on each other, but Prochazka was slightly more aggressive. Stirling also briefly hit the deck once, but it was due to a slip, so it wasn't a true knockdown.

While we wait for Prochazka vs. Stirling to start, check out the scorecards for that Vallejos vs. Sterling co-main event.

This should be a great fight at light heavyweight, as former champ Jiri Prochazka takes on surging newcomer Navajo Stirling.

Prochazka (32-6-1), one of the most prolific knockout artists in MMA, will be looking to rebound from a now infamous failed title bid against Carlos Ulberg. Prior to that, he was riding violent knockout wins over top talents in Jamahal Hill and Khalil Rountree Jr.

Stirling, who trains alongside Ulberg at City Kickboxing, is unbeaten at 11-0. His last six wins have occurred in the Octagon, and the most recent was a vicious first-round stoppage of former champ Jan Blachowicz. If he beats Prochazka, he'll be arguably the top contender in the division—though he'll probably have to decide if he's willing to fight a teammate in Ulberg.

After three rounds, Kevin Vallejos has beaten Aljamain Sterling by unanimous decision. The judges were evidently swayed by the fact that he landed the harder shots on the feet, and managed to fend off most of Sterling's takedown attempts.

This is far and away the biggest win of the Argentinian's career—even if a finish eluded him. He's now 19-1 overall, with wins in eight consecutive fights. It remains to be seen if he gets a crack at featherweight champ Alexander Volkanovski next, but he's clearly one of the top contenders in the division.

"I think the only option is Volkanovski," he said in his post-fight interview. "I hope he gives me the opportunity."

In defeat, Sterling slips to 26-6, and 3-2 as a featherweight. Both of his losses in the division have been very close, so there's no reason to assume he's slowing down, but it's going to take some doing if he hopes to challenge for a belt in this weight class.

After three rounds, Sterling and Vallejos go to the scorecards. It was a very close fight, largely because neither man was really able to get any serious offense going. Sterling landed a couple of takedowns and controlled the fight against the cage at times, but Vallejos was generally able to escape quickly. Both guys landed on the feet, but nothing especially impactful.

Sterling had more success in round two, completing a hard-earned takedown, briefly controlling Vallejos in the clinch, and mixing it up better on the feet. While he spent a moment on his back at the end of the round, it still feels like the judges had to score that one for him. Vallejos is throwing bombs, though, and could end this at any moment.

Aljamain Sterling made it through the first round of his fight with Kevin Vallejos—something not many people have done. That said, Vallejos is clearly hunting for the knockout, and so far, Sterling's takedown attempts have come up short. Unless he can tire Vallejos out, he's gonna be in serious danger whenever this fight is on the feet.

Let's see what the former bantamweight champ can make happen in round two.

We've reached the co-main event of the evening: a high-stakes featherweight clash between Aljamain Sterling and Kevin Vallejos.

Sterling (26-5) is a former bantamweight champ, and one of the best fighters in that division's history. He's recently found new life as a featherweight, with decision wins over Youssef Zalal and Brian Ortega behind him. If he wins this fight, there's a good chance it will set up a showdown with reigning champ Alexander Volkanovski, which would be huge, given their championship legacies.

Vallejos (18-1) hasn't accomplished nearly as much as Sterling, but has won seven consecutive fights, including a pair of big KOs against Giga Chikadze and Josh Emmett. His last loss occurred on Contender Series back in 2023, when he gave up a decision to fellow knockout artist Jean Silva.

This is arguably an even more significant fight than the main event, and it should be a lot of fun. Let's get to it.

After his look to Dan Hooker, Brian Ortega announced his retirement in MMA.

"I started this because I came from nothing," he said in his post-fight interview. "I was fuelled by hate and anger, and I don't have that anymore.

"I healed. As of right now, I think that's it."

He's given us some amazing performances over the years, and notably fought twice for the flyweight belt. Hats off to "T-City" on a great career.

Brian Ortega had a much better third round against Dan Hooker, landing some big punches, and threatening with a choke in the final minute of the round. However, Hooker had plenty of third round success too, and after his dominance in rounds one and two, had done more than enough to earn a unanimous decision.

In victory, Hooker is back on track after three straight finish losses. It's got to feel good. He's now 25-15 overall, and is clearly still a tough out for all but the best lightweights.

He called out Max Holloway in his post-fight interview. That's a great fight. Really great.

In defeat, Ortega is now 16-6, and riding three consecutive decision losses.

Hooker had to fight off a takedown attempt in the final minute of round two, but was otherwise in total control of the round, as he pieced Ortega up with jabs and kicks at range. His uppercut is landing too. Ortega is wearing it, and his corner is begging him to leave it all out there in round three.

Dan Hooker is off to a hot start against Brian Ortega. He's chewing the former featherweight title challenger up with kicks at all levels. He's also notably bigger. Ortega is still in the fight but he needs to get going or the win is going to slip away from him.

Ortega Battles Hooker in Lightweight Debut

It's now time for one of the most anticipated fights of the night: a lightweight clash between Dan Hooker and Brian Ortega.

New Zealand's Hooker (24-15) was once a top lightweight, but has had a rough go of late, suffering stoppage losses in his last three fights, most recently a knockout at the hands of Salahdine Parnasse.

Ortega (16-5), a two-time title challenger at featherweight, will be making his debut at lightweight following decision losses to Diego Lopes and Aljamain Sterling. Like Hooker, he'll be out to prove he's still an elite fighter despite his recent results.

This one could go any number of ways. Let's get to it.

Kyoji Horiguchi surrendered multiple takedowns to Asu Almabayev, and spent much of their flyweight fight pressed against the cage, but still managed to win a clear-cut unanimous decision based purely on damage. Almabayev threw almost no strikes in the fight, even when in top position, while the Japanese veteran was constantly punching and attacking with guillotine chokes. It was a bit of an unusual fight, but the judges definitely got it right.

With the win, Horiguchi is back on track after a knockout loss to Manel Kape, who he also holds a knockout win over. Now an impressive 37-6 overall, he is one of the top contenders in the flyweight division. He called for a title shot in his post-fight interview. He deserves it—after Kape takes on champ Joshua Van in January.

In defeat, Almabayev returns to the loss column following a slick submission of Charles Johnson last time out. He's now 24-4 overall, and is sure to get a ton of blowback for his utterly uninspired performance in Qatar.

It's now time for the second flyweight bout of the night, as dangerous Japanese veteran Kyoji Horiguchi takes on Kazakhstan's Asu Almabayev.

Horiguchi (36-6) is a former UFC title challenger, and also a former Bellator and Rizin champ. He's gone 2-1 since returning to the the UFC, most recently suffering a tough KO loss against upcoming title challenger Manel Kape.

Almabayev (24-3) was also recently knocked out by Kape, but has since rebounded with a trio of wins, most recently a rare Suloev Stretch submission against Charles Johnson that really put him on the map as a contender.

This should be a fun, fast, and technical fight.

Ikram Aliskerov was in total control of his middleweight fight with Jared Cannonier, using a significant grappling advantage to complete multiple takedowns and control the former title challenger over three rounds. Cannonier was able to fight out of multiple submission attempts on the ground, but by the time the fight was over, it was obvious the judges would side with Aliskerov.

With his unanimous decision win over Cannonier, Aliskerov has now won four straight fights. This latest victory is probably the biggest of his career to date. He's now a very impressive 19-2 overall.

Cannonier, meanwhile, has now lost five times in six fights, which is obviously not great. Now 18-11, it's fair to say his days as an elite middleweight are over.

The first fight of the main card will be contested at middleweight, with veteran contender Jared Cannonier taking on Russia's Ikram Aliskerov.

Cannonier (18-10) has been mixing it up with the best middleweights in the sport for years, and even fought Israel Adesanya for the title at one point. He's been struggling lately, however, with four losses in his last five fights, most recently a decision defeat against Christian Leroy Duncan.

Aliskerov (18-2) has been floating just outside the ranking for a while, but hasn't really broken through yet—thanks in large part to a tough KO loss to Robert Whittaker a few years back. He'll look to change that with a fourth straight victory at the expense of Cannonier.

They'll be walking out in moments. Here we go.

Teixeira vs. Gaziev left a very bad taste in a lot of our mouths, but Santiago Luna and Aleksandre Topuria ensured it didn't last long. The two bantamweights put on a fantastic fight over three rounds, with Luna landing a lot more, but Topuria landing a lot harder. It was a razor-close contest, but in the end, the judges scored it for Luna.

With the win, the 22-year-old Mexican rebounds from a tough loss to Bryce Mitchell last time out. He's now 9-1 overall, and clearly has a very bright future in the UFC.

Topuria now stands at 7-1 overall, and loses for the first time since joining the UFC. While he will definitely want to up his volume going forward—that's the main reason he lost this fight—he still looked great in the Octagon tonight.

The final fight of the undercard will be a fun one at bantamweight, as Mexico's Santiago Luna takes on Georgian Spaniard Aleksandra Topuria.

Luna (8-1) has gone 2-1 in the Octagon, most recently losing to Bryce Mitchell via submission in a fight he took on nine days' notice.

Topuria (7-1), the older brother of former two-division champ Ilia, has won his first two fights in the Octagon, defeating Colby Thickness and Bekzat Almakhan by decision. He may not ever reach his brother's level—largely because he spends so much time serving as his brother's coach—but he's an incredibly slick and well-rounded fighter who will be looking to make a statement in Qatar.

Anytime two low-ranked heavyweights collide in the Octagon, there's a good chance it will devolve into a slow, three-round stinker. That's unfortunately what happened in Tallison Teixeira and Shamil Gaziev's undercard meeting.

In a fight with almost no memorable moments, Brazil's Teixeira walked away with a unanimous decision win, probably because he landed quite a few kicks to his opponent's midsection.

He's now 10-2 overall, and back on track after a knockout loss to Sergei Pavlovich. Gaziev slips to 15-4, and returns to the loss column after a knockout win over Kennedy Nzechukwu.

Up next, we've got an Octagon-shaking showdown between Bahrain's Shamil Gaziev and Brazil's Tallison Teixeira.

Gaziev (15-3) has been hovering on the edge of the heavyweight top-15 for years, but has been too inconsistent to assert himself as a serious contender. At present, he's riding a vicious knockout win over Kennedy Nzechukwu.

Teixeira (9-2) has also worked his way to the edge of contender status, but hasn't quite managed to break through, thanks in large part to knockout losses to Derick Lewis and Sergei Pavlovich in his last three fights.

Amir Albazi was in big trouble in the early phases of his rematch with Alessandro Costa, nearly succumbing to a barrage of strikes in round two, and also losing a point for an illegal fence grab.

Just when it was looking like his best case scenario was a draw, he turned things around in round three, tapping his opponent with a rear-naked choke. It's the first time Costa has ever tapped out.

"I have the dog in me," Albazi said in his post-fight interview. "You better knock me clean out to get me out of here."

With the win, which ranks among the best of his UFC career, Albazi is now 18-4. He's now back on track following a decision loss to Kyoji Horiguchi.

Costa, who has now been finished by Albazi twice, falls to 17-6 and has a three-fight snapped.

Next up is the first of two flyweight fights on the bill. This one will be a rematch, pitting Amir Albazi of Iraq against Alessandro Costa of Brazil.

Albazi (17-3), who knocked Costa out in their first meeting in 2022, was once closing in on flyweight title contention. However, he has recently had his momentum derailed by decision losses to Brandon Moreno and Kyoji Horiguchi.

Costa sports a similar pro record of 17-5. Unlike Albazi, he's had great results of late, winning three straight fights by finish, most recently choking out Cody Durden.

Tahir Abdullayev faced a tough test against Jake Matthews, but passed it with flying colours, outwrestling his experienced opponent to a justified unanimous decision win.

That brings the Azerbaijani welterweight to 23-3 overall, and 2-0 in the Octagon. Those are excellent numbers, but he definitely loses some points for missing weight for this fight.

Matthews, who was competing in his 25th UFC fight, is back in the loss column after a decision win over Carlston Harris. He's now 23-9 overall, and will surely be pretty disappointed in his showing in Qatar.

Next on the docket is a 172-pound catchweight clash between Australian veteran Jake Matthews and Azerbaijani prospect Tahir Abdullayev.

Matthews (23-8) has spent years proving he can hang with all but the best welterweights in the UFC. He's currently riding a decision win over Carlston Harris, which was preceded by a fairly surprising submission loss to Neil Magny.

Abdullayev (22-3), who missed weight for this fight, knocked out Jefferson Nascimento in his UFC debut this summer. This can safely be called the toughest test of his career to date. Let's see if he's up to the challenge.

Dom Mar Fan seemed to hit a new level in his lightweight clash with Nikolas Motta. The Aussie was in total control of the fight on the feet and on the mat, and landed enough in both positions that Motta's face was absolutely mangled heading into round three. A corner stoppage seemed possible by that point, but the Brazilian was allowed to return for the final frame and remarkably survived to the scorecards.

With his clear-cut unanimous decision win, Mar Fan is now 10-3 overall, and back on track after a knockout loss to Kody Steele last time out. Clearly, his recent move to City Kickboxing is paying off.

Motta, who unfortunately took an incredible amount of damage in this fight, has now lost two straight following a KO loss to Nazim Sadykhov. He's now 16-7 overall.

It's now time for another lightweight matchup, as Nikolas Motta of Brazil takes on Dom Mar Fan from Australia.

Motta (15-6) has been in the UFC for over five years, but has been very inconsistent, most recently losing to Nazim Sadykhov by KO.

Mar Fan (9-3), who earned his contract through Asia's Road to UFC program, has gone 1-1 in the Octagon, most recently losing to Kody Steele by KO.

After their recent stoppage losses, both guys have a lot to prove in Qatar. Let's get to it.

The UFC's visit to Qatar is off to a hot start, with two knockouts in a row to start the broadcast.

The latest came courtesy of Kazakhstan's Diyar Nurgozhav, who dropped Alik Lorenz with a head-kick in round two of their light heavyweight fight, then finished things with a volley of punches on the ground.

That brings the Kazakh prospect to 13-2 overall. He's now won three straight fights in the UFC, which is particularly impressive given that he lost his first two with the promotion. He's definitely a light heavyweight to keep an eye on.

Lorenz is now 8-3 overall, and will have to wait for his first UFC win.

Next up, two light heavyweight prospects will collide, as Kazakhstan's Diyar Nurgozhay takes on visiting American Alik Lorenz.

Nurgozhay (12-2) won his UFC contract on Contender Series, and has since gone 2-2 in the Octagon, losing his first two appearances by submission, then bouncing back with a decision and a knockout win.

Lorenz (8-2) will be making his UFC debut following a knockout win on Contender Series in August.

Ireland's John Mitchell made quite a splash in his UFC debut, knocking out his former training partner Shoaib Yousaf with a deftly timed knee in round one.

In victory, Mitchell is now 12-3, and 1-0 in the UFC. The future looks bright for him.

Yousaf is now 14-4, and has a six-fight streak derailed by the loss.

Today's UFC card in Qatar is officially underway.

In a few short minutes, we'll kick things off with a clash of lightweight prospects, as Ireland's John Mitchell takes on England's Shoaib Yousaf.

Mitchell (11-3), a PFL veteran, will be making his UFC debut following a first-round KO on the regional circuit.

Yousaf (14-3), a former champ in England's FightStar promotion, will also be making his debut. He's won six straight fights, and has scored knockouts in his last three.

UFC Fight Night: Prochazka vs. Stirling will kick off in a little less than 15 minutes.

There are 12 fights on the bill. Here's what we've got to look forward to.

articles.body: Derrota en Qatar. Aleksandre Topuria (7-2) sufrió en Doha su primer tropiezo en UFC. Tras dos victorias en sus dos primeros combates, el mexicano Santiago Luna (9-1) lo superó y se impuso por decisión dividida (30-27, 28-29 y 29-28) en una pelea muy cerrada. Acompañado en la esquina por su hermano Ilia, Javi Climent y Guram Kutateladze, Aleksandre fue de menos a más en un combate tremendamente estratégico. Luna salió con fuerza buscando lucir su boxeo mexicano y acortar la distancia. Acorralaba a 'Sandro'... pero las primeras manos de poder real le entraron al hispanogeorgiano. Mandó al suelo a Luna con un 'knockdown' y lo puso a temblar. No finalizó en el primer round pero era claramente del mayor de los Topuria. Aleksandre lucía, como siempre, un gran cabeceo y una muy buena defensa, su pateó abajo derribaba a Luna en el inicio del segundo asalto... pero el mexicano es un peleador durísimo y su derrota ante Bryce Mitchell, la última, no lo ha minimizado. Su volumen de golpeo era altísimo y aunque Aleksandre encontraba buenos golpes, Luna parecía incansable. El 1-1 a la hora del llegar al tercer round era claro. Y ahí, en los últimos cinco minutos, se impuso una vez más el volumen de golpeo de Luna. El peleador mexicano superó a un Aleksandre que, para sorpresa de todos, no buscó el derribo en ningún momento. Incluso en algunas acciones en las que parecía que podía llevar la pelea al suelo, tras reducirse la distancia y agarrarse ambos peleadores, volvía a buscar el 'striking'. Aleksandre, de 30 años (cumplirá 31 a finales de enero), ve frenado así su ascenso en el peso gallo, quedándose a las puertas de una posible entrada al top-15.

Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live THIS MORNING (Sat., Nov. 21, 2026) with UFC Qatar , streaming live online via Paramount+ . The event takes place inside ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar. Our main event for this early morning card is Jiri Prochazka vs. Navajo Stirling in UFC's Light Heavyweight division.

UFC is closing out 2026 with a Middle East swing and then a home game at T-Mobile Arena. The first of those Middle East shows is this weekend in Doha, Qatar. This the promotion's second time in Qatar, following the Arman Tsarukyan vs. Dan Hooker -led card we had last year.

This time there's two potential title eliminator bouts on tap in the desert. The main event could generate the next opponent for recovering UFC Light Heavyweight champion, Carlos Ulberg ( those details here ). That fight pits his last opponent, Jiri Prochazka , against his City Kickboxing teammate, Navajo Stirling .

Prochazka hasn't competed since Ulberg knocked him out on one leg ( re-live that here ). Stirling is getting a relatively short turnaround after KOing Jan Blachowicz in August ( watch it ).

The co-main is Aljamain Sterling vs. Kevin Vallejos . Sterling just took out a rising prospect in the form of Youssef Zalal , and now he'll try and do that again. Vallejos comes in here after starching Josh Emmett . The winner of this one might end up in a Featherweight title fight, especially if Alexander Volkanovski vacates the belt so he can chase Lightweight gold.

Dan Hooker is back in Qatar this weekend. He's welcoming Brian Ortega to the Lightweight division. The main card also has Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev in a key Flyweight bout. Jared Cannonier vs. Ikram Aliskerov rounds out the card.

The featured "Prelims" bout is Aleksandre Topuria vs. Santiago Luna . The shorter than usual card also has Shamil Gaziev vs. Tallison Teixeira , Amir Albazi vs. Alessandro Costa 2, Jake Matthews vs. Tahir Abdullayev , Niklos Motta vs. Dom Mar Fan , Diyar Nurgozhay vs. Alik Lorenzb and Shoaib Yousaf vs. John Mitchell.

We're watching fights over coffee this morning, if you are in on US east coast time like me. Here are the times for each portion of today's UFC Qatar card:

UFC Qatar "Prelims" will begin at 1o a.m. ET .

UFC Qatar main card is scheduled to start at 1 p.m. ET .

All of UFC Qatar airs on Paramount+ , which you can stream here .

The live blog here starts rolling below at 10 a.m. ET . Come in and say hi!

205 lbs.: Jiri Prochazka vs. Navajo Stirling

145 lbs.: Kevin Vallejos def. Aljamain Sterling by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

155 lbs.: Dan Hooker def. Brian Ortega by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27) — HIGHLIGHTS

125 lbs.: Kyoji Horiguchi def. Asu Almabayev by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

155 lbs.: John Mitchell def. Shoaib Yousaf by KO (knee and punches), round 1 (3:50) – HIGHLIGHTS

Round 1: Sterling shoots, but Vellajos fights it off. Sterling backs up and out of range. Vallejos lands a one-two, but Sterling is moving backwards. When Sterling steps in to throw a leg kick, Vallejos is throwing power punches and Sterling has to back-up. Vallejos sprawls to avoid a takedown. Vallejos sprawls to block another takedown. A lot of respect here, from both men, and that means we're seeing a lot of caution. Vallejos doesn't want to throw and miss and get taken down and Sterling doesn't want to get flatlined.

Round 2: Sterling manages to get into Vallejos' body and out of range of his power punches. He struggles to get Vallejos down, though. Sterling has him on the fence, but Vallejos is able to rotate and separate. Sterling takes a big swing and a miss on a punch. Sterling lands a body kick. He's looking more aggressive now. Vallejos catches Sterling as he shoots. Sterling slumps back, he might have been stung. Vallejos gets on top of him. Sterling manages to get up and they both miss on some bigf shots.

Round 3: Sterling throws more body kicks. Vallejos lands a low kick. Vallejos misses on a punch and gets taken down. He rolls and manages to get back on his feet, though. Sterling lands a leg kick and then a straight punch. Nothing he's landing is making much impact. Vallejos lands another short punch when Sterling dives in. Sterling shoots again and almost eats a knee. Vallejos hops away from him again. Sterling holds Vallejos against the fence. Sterling tries to peel him off the fence, but he's finding it hard. Mike Beltran breaks it up. Vallejos throws a right and Sterling spins with an elbow, neither land. Vallejos sprawls and lands an uppercut. Sterling gets a single leg and takes Vallejos back to the fence. Every round is close, but I think Vallejos won them all.

Official decision: Kevin Vallejos def. Aljamain Sterling by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

Round 1: Hooker lands some kicks to the legs and body early on. Hooker just misses on a head kick. He flashes that head kick again. He's getting close on that. Hooker buckles Ortega on a calf kick. Hooker is just teeing off on kicks. He's got no respect for Ortega's striking. Ortega times a good shot while Hooker is kicking, he gets him down, but allows too much space and Hooker is back up. Ortega lands a good punch to the body.

Round 2: Ortega lands some nice punches to start this round. That's made Hooker ditch some of kicks. He's throwing punches now. Ortega slides in for a single leg, but he can't get Hooker down. Hooker lands an uppercut. Ortega lands an overhand right. Ortega is starting to wear some of these punches. Hooker lands another good calf kick. Ortega tries to throw a short upwards elbow, but misses. Hooker drifts out of range of punches and then lands a nice combo. Ortega gets deep on a single leg, but Hooker stays up on the fence.

Round 3: Ortega's corner tries to fire him up. Everyone knows he needs a finish. Hooker lands more calf kicks. Ortega puts his chin down and walks forwards. He's throwing some shots, but not many and Hooker is countering each time. The pace ups a little and both land hard punches. The momentum starts to build and we get another big exchange of combos. Ortega is really pushing. Hooker lands a knee to the body. Ortega lands a big right hook. He can't keep the pace up, though. We slow back down to single shots and one-twos being exchanged. Ortega shoots, but can't get the takedown. What's the point in even doing that? The best he can do is take the round with it, but not win the fight. He gets Hooker down and tries an arm triangle, but there's no time left.

Official decision: Dan Hooker def. Brian Ortega by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

Round 1: Lots of distance between these two for the first minute of the round. Both man throwing at air. Horiguchi steps in and lands some jabs. He then knocks out one of Almabayev's legs with a kick. Almabayev gets right up. Horiguchi misses on a combo. Almabayev lands a spin kick to the body. He misses on a big punch and Horiguchi gets a body lock. He gets behind Almabayev. Almabayev tries to escape on the fence. Horiguchi abandons the position. Almabayev lands a big inside leg kick. Then misses on a high kick. Horiguchi kicks the body and Almabaev turns that into a takedown. He stacks the legs. Horiguchi tries a guillotine. He's not putting a lot of power into it, though. Horiguchi now starts to squeeze. Almabayev pops his head out.

Round 2: Horiguchi leans in and lands a right hand. Almabayev drops and gets a nice takedown. Horiguchi scrambles to the fence. Almabayev tries to work an angle to get on the back, but Horiguchi is able to defend that for a good minute. Almabayev eventually drops back and gets Horiguchi away from the fence. Horiguchi is able to stand, though. Almabayev sticks to him on the fence and Horiguchi jumps the guillotine. He lets it go tries to build to his feet. Horiguchi lands punches from the bottom. Almabayev has thrown nothing. Horiguchi wins the round despite being in the bottom position.

Round 3: Horiguchi darts in with a punch, but Almabayev perfectly times hi level change and lands a takedown. Horiguchi explodes and sweeps, though. Horiguchi stands and lands some good punches. Almabayev dives and gets another takedown. Horiguchi lands elbows and then hits the same sweep. Almabayev grabs the fence. Horiguchi separates. Almabayev shoots again and eventually gets Horiguchi down by the fence. Horiguchi goes for the guillotine again. Almabayev pops his head out and Horiguchi tries to elbow his head off when he does. He half lands that and may have split Almabayev open with it. Almabayev continues to work his top position but is doing literally nothing else.

Official decision: Kyoji Horiguchi def. Asu Almabayev by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

Round 1: Cannonier takes the center and tries to stalk Aliskerov. Aliskerov circles and seems hesitant to pull the trigger. Cannonier lands a good jab. Cannonier attacks and tries to clinch Aliskerov up against the fence, Aliskerov backs out of trouble, though. Aliskerov finally steps forwards and lands a one two, that hurt Cannonier. Cannonier goes down, off a slip perhaps, but eats a big knee to the body on the way back up. Aliskerov more confident now. He has the center and is popping his jab out there.

Round 2: Aliskerov continues on from the last round, taking the center and threatening with his jab. Cannonier extends to respond and Aliskerov ducks under and gets the takedown. Cannonier manages to scoot to the cage, but Aliskerov gets full mount once he gets there. The referee stands them up, though. Aliskerov is penalised for grabbing the fence. Just a warning. Aliskerov catches Cannonier's leg and tips him onto the ground. He jumps on an arm triangle attempt. Cannonier fights that off, but Aliskerov is all over him. He gets full mount again. Cannonier gets back to half guard. Aliskerov tries to take the back. Cannonier stands as Aliskerov tries to get under his chin.

Round 3: Cannonier pushes early, trying to land a big shot over the top. Aliskerov looks a little tired. Aliskerov shoots and gets the takedown by the fence. Aliskerov steps over and tries a kimura. Cannonier is too strong, though. He turns and starts to stand. Aliskerov tries to ride him, but can't get the back. Aliskerov changes levels and gets another takedown. He gets the back, with a body triangle. Cannonier is too tough to choke out, but Aliskerov banks the round.

Official decision: Ikram Aliskerov def. Jared Cannonier by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

Aleksandre Topuria vs. Santiago Luna: These two treated us to a very technical mostly boxing match. Luna brought the volume, landing a record breaking amount of strikes, and Topuria brought the power with his single shots (overhand right and an outside leg kick). As the fight went on, the volume kept adding up and the latter rounds were more obviously won by Luna.

Official decision: Santiago Luna def. Aleksandre Topuria by split decision (30-27, 28-29, 29-28)

Shamil Gaziev vs. Tallison Teixeira: That was one of those terrible heavyweight fights we get served up every now and then. Very little happened here and neither guy deserved a W on their record. I thought Gaziev did marginally more and should have gotten the decision, but it's hard to get mad when the fight is that bad.

Official decision: Tallison Teixeira def. Shamil Gaziev by unanimous decision (30-27, 29-28, 29-28)

Amir Albazi vs. Alessandro Costa: Albazi showed a ton of grit in this one. He took the first round on Costa and was almost finished in the second. He was docked a point for a fence grab in the second, while he survived Costa's attempt to hunt for a finish. In the second Albazi's wrestling took over again and we were on course for a draw until Albazi snatched up a rear naked choke. He's now 2-0 against Costa.

Official decision: Amir Albazi def. Alessandro Costa by submission (rear naked choke), round 3 (4:34)

Jake Matthews vs. Tahir Abdullayev: Abdullayev hurt Matthews on the feet in the first round and then spent much of the second and third laying on top of him. Matthews fell in love with going for submissions off his back. But his gogoplata and triangle attempts weren't close to finishing Abdullayev and they didn't win him any scorecards either. They also let the tried Abdullayev spend a lot more time on top, while not producing much offense.

Official decision: Tahir Abdullayev def. Jake Matthews by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

Dom Mar Fan vs. Nikolas Motta: Dom Mar Fan rearranged Nikolas Motta's face. He took him down in the second and caused a ton of damage with ground and pound. Motta responded with a knockdown in the second round, but Fan used his grappling to survive. These two traded a bunch on the feet after that and Fan landed some massive shots that opened up all kinds of cuts on Motta's poor face.

Official decision: Dom Mar Fan def. Nikolas Motta by unanimous decision (30-26, 30-26, 29-27)

Diyar Nurgozhay vs. Alik Lorenz: Nurgozhay and Lorenz had a fun back and forth brawl in the first round. Nurgozhay looked like the more polished and UFC ready product, though. In the second Nugozhay sliced Lorenz with a head kick and then put him away with punches.

Official decision: Diyar Nurgozhay def. Alik Lorenz by TKO (head kick and punches), round 2 (0:24)

John Mitchell vs. Shoaib Yousaf: The hastily put together battle of journeymen finished in the first round. The commentary team was loving on Shoaib Yousaf, but the better tested John Mitchell patiently went about his work and eventually put Yousaf down with a big knee and follow up punches.

Official decision: John Mitchell def. Shoaib Yousaf by KO (knee and punches), round 1 (3:50)

articles.title: Kevin Vallejos decisions Aljamain Sterling in UFC Qatar co-main event
articles.summary: Featherweight contenders Aljamain Sterling and Kevin Vallojos met in the UFC Qatar co-main event.
articles.body:
Former bantamweight champion Aljamain Sterling continued his quest to make a run at the featherweight championship on Saturday in the UFC Qatar co-main event. Ranked No. 4 in the division, Sterling faced No. 9 ranked Kevin Vallejos .

Sterling entered the bout coming off back-to-back wins and on the cusp of fighting for a second divisional title. Vallejos made the walk to the octagon carrying a seven-fight winning streak and looking to pick up the biggest win of his career.

Sterling took the center of the cage and targeted Vallejos' body with a kick. He changed levels but was unable to secure the takedown. Vallejos stepped in the pocket with a left hand while Sterling invested in leg kicks. Vallejos defended another takedown attempt. Vallejos pressed forward as Sterling circled on the outside. Sterling wasn't fully committing to the takedowns but mixed them in. MMAWeekly scored the round 10-9 for Sterling.

Sterling went to thebody with a kick and Vallejos responded with a left hand. A right hand landed for Vallejos. Sterling answered with a leg kick and secured the first takedown of the fight. Vallejos quickly got back to his feet but they remained in the clinch. Along the cage, Sterling delivered knees the body. They separated and Sterling landed his jab followed by a back kick to the body. Vallejos pressed forward with a right hand. Sterling attempted a takedown and ended up on the bottom. He let Sterling up and they exchanged shots to the body. MMAWeekly scored the round 10-9 for Vallejos.

Vallejos inched forward to start the final frame. Sterling briefly secured a takedown but couldn't keep Vallejos grounded. Vallejos connected with a left hand and stuffed a takedown attempt. Sterling clinched after absorbing a right hand. They worked for position along the fence at the round's midway mark. The referee separated them with 80 seconds left on the clock. Sterling worked for a takedown late. The fight ended with the two battling in the clinch. MMAWeekly scored the round 10-9 for Vallejos.

The Judges scored the fight for Vallejos via unanimous decision. The scorecards read 30–27, 30–27, and 29–28.

articles.title: UFC Qatar: Rising star Navajo Stirling knocks out Jiri Prochazka
articles.summary: Rising star Navajo Stirling earns the biggest win of his career as he knocks out former champion Jiri Prochazka in the second round at UFC Qatar.
articles.body:
Rising star Navajo Stirling earned the biggest win of his career as he knocked out former champion Jiri Prochazka in the second round at UFC Qatar.

New Zealand light-heavyweight Stirling stopped Prochazka with a clean right hook to extend the unbeaten start to his career to 12 fights.

Victory marked the 29-year-old's fourth straight win in 2026, all by knockout, as he strengthened his claim to be the UFC's fighter of the year.

Stirling's form, coupled with beating 34-year-old Czech Prochazka in such convincing fashion, would usually open the door to a title shot, but there remains an obstacle to the fight happening.

The light-heavyweight champion is Stirling's team-mate, Carlos Ulberg, who trains at the same gym in New Zealand.

When asked who he'd like to fight next, Sterling said: "I'm not too sure yet, we'll figure something out and see who's above me."

It's rare for fighters to compete against their training partners, with whom they form close friendships in the gym.

Ulberg beat Prochazka for the light-heavyweight title in April, but has not fought since after tearing his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) during the contest.

Prochazka, who has won 32 of his 40 professional fights, was regarded as the toughest test of Stirling's four-year career, but he looked comfortable against the former champion.

He peppered Prochazka with leg kicks in the early stages, before waiting for his moment to strike in the second round.

After dodging a punch, Stirling countered with a right hook which sent Prochazka to the canvas, before the referee rushed in to stop the contest after a follow-up strike on the ground.

After the fight, Prochazka conceded Stirling was "the better fighter" on the night, as the New Zealander celebrated with his team-mates inside the octagon.

Ireland's Mitchell earns impressive debut KO

On the undercard, Ireland's John Mitchell made a statement in his first UFC fight as he knocked out fellow debutant Shoaib Yousaf.

The pair took the fight on only four days' notice but it was Mitchell who triumphed after dropping his British opponent with a knee in the first round.

Victory extends 31-year-old Mitchell's record to 12 wins and three defeats.

After the fight, he revealed he nearly lost his foot last year after requiring three surgeries on an injury.

"It's mad, this time in December last year I had three surgeries on my foot and thought I was gonna lose the foot. But we didn't lose it, so happy days," said Mitchell.

Elsewhere, former featherweight title contender Brian Ortega announced his retirement after defeat by Dan Hooker.

Ortega, 35, fought Max Holloway for the featherweight belt in 2019 and Alexander Volkanovski for the title in 2021, losing both fights.

The American leaves the sport having won 16 of his 23 fights since debuting in 2010, with eight of those victories coming via submission and three by knockout.

"I wanted to do this because I came from nothing and I wanted to do something and I was fuelled by hate and by anger," said Ortega.

"And I don't have that any more. I healed, so as of right now, I think this is it."

articles.title: Dos Santos noquea a Rodríguez y 'Wasabi' se retira a lo grande en WOW 34 Valencia
articles.standfirst: El peleador español puso el broche de oro a una carrera de leyenda con una victoria ante César Arzamendia y un bonito homenaje
articles.summary: El peleador español puso el broche de oro a una carrera de leyenda con una victoria ante César Arzamendia y un bonito homenaje
articles.body: WOW FC ha vuelto a Valencia y al Roig Arena por todo lo alto con WOW 34, otra cartelera en la que cerca de 14.000 espectadores de han vuelto a juntar en este emblemático recinto para disfrutar de una velada llena de acción y grandes momentos. En el combate estelar, Felipe Dos Santos (12-3) ha finalizado a Luis Iván Rodríguez (11-3) en el primer asalto para poner el broche de oro a un evento lleno de emociones a flor de piel. El peleador brasileño del 'Chute Box' llegaba a WOW FC después de su paso por la UFC, y demostró su nivel de élite con un K.O. al hígado gracias a una patada estando en el suelo que sorprendió a Rodríguez. Al terminar, Fabià Sintes subió al octágono para anunciar que dejaba vacante el cinturón de peso mosca, por lo que Felipe puede ser el próximo retador. Además, en rueda de prensa le dedicó unas bonitas palabras a Allan Nascimento, su compañero de gimnasio fallecido recientemente. En el combate co estelar Enrique 'Wasabi' Marín (15-8) se ha retirado por todo lo alto tras finalizar su combate ante César 'Goku' Arzamendia (9-8), que no quiso salir al segundo asalto después de recibir un knockdowns y bastante daño en el primer round. Después de ser un pionero en las MMA españolas y convertirse en leyenda, 'Wasabi' recibió un emotivo homenaje y una despedida a la altura de su figura, convirtiéndose en el primer 'imborrable' de WOW FC y primer Hall of Fame de la compañía tras recibir una placa conmemorativa y decir adiós entre lágrimas. Mor Dieye (6-0) también hizo los deberes venciendo a Timur Kurbankadiev (7-2) por decisión unánime después de un gran despliegue físico como suele acostumbrar. Además, acto seguido cogió el micrófono y pidió al ganador del duelo que habrá en WOW 35 Madrid el próximo 12 de diciembre entre Umakhan Ibragimov y Nick Fiore por el cinturón de peso ligero. Sin duda ha hecho méritos para ello. David Hervías (4-0) fue otro de los nombres que brilló con luz propia, ya que sometió a Luis Hernández (6-2) en menos de un minuto para demostrar por qué es uno de los mayores prospectos de las MMA españolas. El peleador del gimnasio 'The Black Panther' ni siquiera lanzó un golpe, ya que derribo a su rival rápidamente y transicionó al triángulo de brazo para dar motivos a WOW FC de crear un cinturón en el peso medio. Una de las actuaciones de la noche fue la de Mouslim Saidoulaiev (1-0), que debutó en profesional por todo lo alto conectando una increíble patada frontal a Adonis Montero (0-2) y finalizándole a posteriori con una llave de brazo. Dimitri Barkaia (2-0) también protagonizó una gran actuación ante Michele Balducci (1-2), ya que después de sufrir en el primer round logró un mataleón en el segundo tras dañar a su rival con el striking. Otro evento para el recuerdo que vuelve a demostrar por qué las MMA españolas están en auge y WOW FC en concreto, que no para de superarse a sí misma y lo ha demostrado llenando prácticamente el Roig Arena a pesar de no tener ningún peleador local en el evento estelar. El límite es el cielo.

articles.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have a genuine animosity, says Olympic gold medallist Audley Harrison | 'We need to see it'
articles.summary: Audley Harrison doesn't believe Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua has been left too late in their careers; "they're not in their primes but there's still enough there and the animosity that they have is genuine. So it's a fight definitely I want to see," the Olympic gold medallist said
articles.body:
Harrison was one half of an all-British heavyweight grudge match when he boxed David Haye in a 2010 event that was much hyped but ultimately disappointed.

Harrison though doesn't think Fury and Joshua have left their fight too late.

"'Politricks' has always been there in boxing, always unfortunately messing up boxing," Harrison told Sky Sports .

"I will be sitting on the edge of my seat for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. They're not in their primes but there's still enough there and the animosity that they have is genuine. So it's a fight definitely I want to see. While it's a little late, I can't argue with that.

"It's not going to be them in their primes but it's going to be good enough. We need to see it for sure."

He added: "Look at Mike Tyson-Lennox Lewis, everyone was complaining for that fight, that fight was like five years too late in many people's eyes.

"I was there in Memphis, it was a great fight, great atmosphere, exactly what we wanted.

"Lennox banged him out but the fight was so exciting."

Harrison preceded Joshua as an Olympic super-heavyweight gold medallist for Great Britain. But he did not scale the heights Joshua achieved in the professional ranks. Joshua has twice been a unified heavyweight world champion and has made a habit of selling out stadium shows in London and Cardiff.

"All of these guys came from nowhere. AJ went to the Olympics not as the favourite, same as Deontay Wilder, and they punched their way to glory," Harrison said.

"When Joshua turned pro he was raw as hell, you've got to give him credit he was able to go through.

"When he lost to [Andy] Ruiz they crucified him because he was meant to win, but he was still raw. He's always been really disciplined, he's strong and he's always come into the ring ready.

"Technically and tactically he's been off in some fights, obviously with [Oleksandr] Usyk, obviously with [Daniel] Dubois. But came back in the [Wladimir] Klitschko fight. When you look at his career, you've got to take your hat off. He wasn't perfect, but he's not supposed to be."

Harrison added: "He's still got the power, he's still got the punch but he doesn't have the punch resistance now.

"We're seeing that with Joshua, we're seeing that with Fury. We haven't seen that with Usyk yet. I haven't seen him start to flounder yet in terms of punch resistance.

"To be fair to AJ and Tyson Fury, they've both had a legendary career, when you look at what they've done, not just the money they've made, if you look at their legacy."

articles.title: Topuria sale en defensa de su hermano y lanza un mensaje a sus críticos: "Que os jodan"
articles.standfirst: La estrella de la UFC asegura que su hermano Aleksandre se dislocó el hombro durante la pelea con el mexicano Luna
articles.summary: La estrella de la UFC asegura que su hermano Aleksandre se dislocó el hombro durante la pelea con el mexicano Luna
articles.body: Ilia Topuria ha salido al paso tras la primera derrota de su hermano Aleksandre en la UFC, que cayó este sábado por decisión dividida ante el mexicano Santiago Luna en el UFC Qatar celebrado en Doha, para explicar lo ocurrido en el octágono y cargar con dureza contra las críticas. El combate de peso gallo, que cerraba la cartelera preliminar, dejó a un Aleksandre irreconocible tras un buen primer asalto, frenando en seco la racha de dos victorias que acumulaba hasta ahora en la compañía. A través de un comunicado en sus redes sociales, el luchador hispanogeorgiano ha revelado que una luxación en el hombro izquierdo al inicio frustró por completo a su hermano, impidiéndole buscar derribos o lanzar combinaciones con normalidad. "La respuesta es sencilla: no estábamos viendo al Aleks que todos conocemos. Estábamos viendo a un guerrero intentando competir con un hombro dislocado", ha explicado Ilia, poniendo en valor que aguantara los tres asaltos pese a tener la guardia mermada: "Para mí, eso dice mucho más de él que cualquier resultado". Además, aunque ha felicitado a Luna por el triunfo, no ha ocultado su espina clavada: "No puedo evitar preguntarme qué habría pasado si mi hermano hubiera podido luchar al 100%". La estrella de la UFC también ha cargado sin filtros contra quienes han aprovechado el tropiezo para atacar a su familia. "Cuando se trata de mi hermano, no voy a permanecer en silencio", ha advertido antes de arremeter contra sus detractores: "Centraos en construir vuestras propias vidas. La envidia, la amargura y el odio que proyectáis sobre los demás no dicen nada de nosotros. Lo revelan todo sobre el mundo que lleváis dentro". Más contundente aún se ha mostrado con quienes, según denuncia, se aprovecharon de ambos en el pasado: "Durante años, muchas personas han intentado aprovecharse de nosotros. Y en lugar de mostrar siquiera un mínimo de gratitud por lo que hemos hecho por ellas, algunas han elegido difundir mierda y hablar mal de nosotros a nuestras espaldas". Su dardo final no dejó lugar a dudas: "Y si estáis leyendo esto preguntándoos si estoy hablando de vosotros, probablemente sí. Que os jodan". Por último, Ilia ha cerrado su mensaje con un respaldo absoluto a Aleksandre: "Hermano, no podría estar más orgulloso de ti. De tu trabajo duro, de tu corazón y de tu capacidad para seguir adelante cuando todo se vuelve en tu contra". Tras recordar que "una derrota no define a un hombre. Lo hace la manera en la que se levanta después", dejó una advertencia para el próximo curso: "Y nosotros siempre nos levantamos. 2027, vamos a por todo".

articles.title: Isabel Rivero hace historia y unifica dos cinturones mundiales
articles.standfirst: Derrotó por puntos en decisión unánime a la campeona mundial IBF, la japonesa Sumire Yamanaka, y se convierte en el primer boxeador español en unificar dos cinturones
articles.summary: Derrotó por puntos en decisión unánime a la campeona mundial IBF, la japonesa Sumire Yamanaka, y se convierte en el primer boxeador español en unificar dos cinturones
articles.body: Histórica. Isabel Rivero, campeona mundial WBA del peso átomo, se convirtió este sábado en el primer boxeador español en unificar dos cinturones mundiales. En una abarrotada Plaza de Toros de Illescas (Toledo), derrotó por puntos en decisión unánime a la campeona mundial IBF, la japonesa Sumire Yamanaka (10-2, 3 KO), con puntuaciones de 97-93, 96-94 y 96-94. En categoría femenina, no era la primera vez que una española disputaba más de un cinturón mundial- Ya lo hicieron Miriam Gutiérrez en 2020, Mary Romero en 2024 o Jennifer Miranda en 2025, pero no lo lucharon en España, ni tampoco eran campeonas, por lo que no pudieron conseguir ninguna la victoria. Isabel Rivero, científica de profesión, se alzó con su primer cinturón hace menos de un año. Entonces derrotó por KO a la mexicana Silvia Torres. Seis meses después defendió ese cinturón ante la Tailandesa Watcharaporn Namphon.

articles.title: Aleksandre Topuria se lesionó en el primer round de UFC Qatar
articles.standfirst: El hispanogeorgiano perdió por decisión dividida ante Santiago Luna
articles.summary: El hispanogeorgiano perdió por decisión dividida ante Santiago Luna
articles.body: Ayer, ante el mexicano Santiago Luna (9-1), Aleksandre Topuria (7-2) encajó su primera derrota en UFC. Fue por decisión dividida en un combate que, en realidad, ganó claramente su rival (29-28, seguramente)... pero que cambió después del primer 'round', con la lesión de hombro que sufrió el peleador hispanogeorgiano. "En los primeros minutos del combate, mi hermano se dislocó el hombro izquierdo, lo que cambió por completo el rumbo del combate. Muchos se preguntaron por qué no lanzaba combinaciones, no intentaba derribos ni mantenía la guardia alta. La verdad es que no pudimos ver al Aleks que todos conocemos", declaraba hoy su hermano Ilia Topuria, que estaba con él en la esquina, en redes sociales. Aleksandre, que estuvo en el hospital tras el combate para revisar dicha lesión, no pudo mostrar todo su potencial y, de hecho, su 'game plan' se vio demasiado unidimensional a causa de ese problema físico: solamente golpeando con la derecha, acorralado en todo momento y sin intentar en ningún momento los derribos. "A pesar de luchar con un hombro dislocado y verse obligado a abandonar su estrategia de combate, consiguió llevar el combate hasta una decisión dividida. Eso por sí solo dice mucho de su coraje. No siento más que respeto por su rival, pero no puedo evitar preguntarme qué habría pasado si mi hermano hubiera estado al 100%", añadió un Ilia Topuria que, después del combate, felicitó a Santiago Luna por su gran triunfo.

articles.title: Ilia Topuria: "Este año nos ha enseñado a los dos que incluso los guerreros mejor preparados pueden caer"
articles.standfirst: Así fue el mensaje del 'Matador' a su hermano tras la derrota en UFC Qatar
articles.summary: Así fue el mensaje del 'Matador' a su hermano tras la derrota en UFC Qatar
articles.body: Sin duda alguna, 2026 ha sido el peor año posible en lo deportivo para los hermanos Topuria. Ilia perdió su invicto en UFC Casa Blanca ante Gaethje, sufriendo además graves lesiones que lo tendrán fuera de la jaula casi un año (quiere volver en abril); ayer, por otro lado, Aleksandre perdió por decisión dividida con Santiago Luna y, también, sufrió una lesión en el hombro izquierdo. Dos derrotas que, pese al impacto que ha tenido en el 'aura de invencibilidad' de ambos (sobre todo en la de Ilia), los hacen, en palabras de los dos, más fuertes y experimentados. Era el propio Ilia el que, tras la derrota de Aleksandre, dejaba un mensaje para su hermano: "Este año nos ha enseñado a los dos que incluso los guerreros mejor preparados pueden caer. Pero también sabemos algo que mucha gente nunca entenderá: una derrota no define a un hombre. Lo que lo define es cómo se levanta después de ella. Y nosotros siempre nos levantaremos". El mayor de los Topuria, en otro comunicado emitido en sus redes sociales, mantiene encendida la llama para volver con más fuerza: "Todo pasa por una razón. Esto es sólo el comienzo".

images.caption: Aleksandre e Ilia Topuria, en UFC Qatar. UFC.

articles.summary: El Conquistador sufrió una luxación en el hombro izquierdo en el primer round

"En los primeros minutos del combate, mi hermano se dislocó el hombro izquierdo, lo que cambió por completo el rumbo del combate. Muchos se preguntaron por qué no lanzaba combinaciones, no intentaba derribos ni mantenía la guardia alta. La verdad es que no pudimos ver al Aleks que todos conocemos", declaraba hoy en redes sociales su hermano Ilia Topuria, que estaba con él en la esquina. Y así fue, a los 40 segundos, en un intercambio con Luna, a Aleksandre se le dislocó el hombro izquierdo. Es decir, peleó 14 minutos y 20 segundos estando lesionado. Pese a ello, 'El Conquistador' superó la presión inicial de Luna y ganó el primer round para dos de los jueces... con 'knockdown' incluido en esos primeros cinco minutos de pelea. Como ha podido saber MARCA, el dolor era muy fuerte y generaba, sobre todo, una gran dificultad de movilidad en ese brazo izquierdo. Por eso Aleksandre vio reducido su 'game plan' a buscar la derecha, defenderse y tirar sus habituales esquivas... sin opción de derribar o encontrar combinaciones más largas y técnicas. Todo el 'game plan' estaba comprometido. El tema ahora es cómo de grave es la lesión y cuándo podría volver a pelear. Todo pasará por la resonancia que se le hará en los próximos días pero la lesión, como cuentan a MARCA, podría ser importante. El propio Aleksandre, mientras, no busca excusas: "No digo esto para quitarle nada a nadie, y mucho menos para justificar el resultado. Simplemente quiero compartir cuál fue mi realidad anoche, porque mucha gente ha estado preguntando, y creo que los que me apoyan merecen saber lo que pasó". Y promete volver más fuerte: "No me arrepiento, y no tengo nada por lo que reprocharme. Acepto lo que pasó con la tranquilidad de saber que lo di todo, como siempre prometo. Todo pasa por una razón. Esto es sólo el comienzo. Gracias a Dios por todo, siempre".
