articles.title: Josh Hokit fans go after referee’s kids following UFC 334: ‘Scared of being called out?’
articles.summary: Marc Goddard is one of the few UFC referees that actually participates on social media from time to time, but he’s locking things down after some extremely c...
articles.body:
Marc Goddard is one of the few UFC referees that actually participates on social media from time to time, but he's locking things down after some extremely creepy messages from anti-social morons on X (formerly Twitter).

Goddard's most recent assignment was the Josh Hokit vs. Ciryl Gane fight at UFC 334 which saw Gane beat Hokit via 49-48×3 unanimous decision. That theoretically could have been 48-48 had Goddard seen an eye poke from Gane on Hokit in the first round and taken a point from the foul-heavy Frenchman. But Goddard didn't see it, and some UFC fans are clearly upset over that.

Shortly after the fight, Goddard set his X account to private, which limits who can see his posts and who can reply.

"You go private cause you're scared of being called out and held accountable for missing a blatant eye poke as the first shot of the fight from someone known for them?" one person asked.

Goddard then replied by sharing a comment from a user stating "I hope your children get hit by a bus and found dead."

"This is just one of the reasons / examples of why I turn of comments & notifications or adjust the settings of my own platforms etc," he replied back. "If that's OK with you?"

"I've had an account here for 17 years," Goddard wrote. "This week was the first time EVER that I turned any form of commenting / interaction off. Scared of being held accountable? I live a professional life of being analyzed, on show, taking 'flak,' abused etc all in the name of trying to make my living."

"Say what you want both to and about me. I'm very well used to that. My eldest children are old enough to have their own social media, my youngest at 11 years old (thankfully) is not."

UFC referees have often been heavily criticized for screwing up, but the intensity of that criticism has ramped up significantly since betting has become a massive part of the sport. Whether you think Goddard is a terrible ref running cover for Gane's obvious cheating or that he just legitimately didn't see the poke, I think we can all agree his children don't deserve to be run over by a bus.

What's interesting here is that Goddard is one of the good ones — not perfect by any means but definitely better than a lot of the do-nothing refs that populate the sport these days. The reason so many fans were upset that Goddard didn't see Gane's eye poke is that Goddard is one of the only refs in the sport that might deduct a point for it. No other ref on rotation that night would have done it other than him. So maybe chill out a bit with the attacks on his family, dorks.

articles.title: Tyson Fury desvela que tiene esquizofrenia: "Viví en lo más profundo del infierno"
articles.standfirst: "Cumplía con todos los requisitos: depresión, ansiedad, trastorno bipolar"
articles.summary: "Cumplía con todos los requisitos: depresión, ansiedad, trastorno bipolar"
articles.body: El boxeador Tyson Fury ha sido diagnosticado con esquizofrenia, según revela su esposa Paris en un documental de Netflix que ha causado gran impacto en el mundo pugilístico. La revelación se ha producido sólo 18 días antes del esperado combate de los pesos pesados de Fury, el 'Rey Gitano del Boxeo', contra Anthony Joshua que se podrá ver en Netflix. La pelea se celebrará el viernes 11 de diciembre de 2026 en el Principality Stadium de Cardiff (Gales), y se cerró tras más de una década de negociaciones y varios intentos fallidos. Ambos llegan a esta cita en la recta final de sus carreras tras haber sido campeones mundiales y sufrir derrotas importantes en los últimos años. Fury salió de su retiro tras caer ante Oleksandr Usyk y sumó victorias frente a Arslanbek Makhmudov y Mariusz Wach. Por su parte Joshua, que sufrió un grave accidente de tráfico en Nigeria a finales de 2025 en el que fallecieron dos amigos, volvió a pelear el 25 de julio de 2026 frente al peso pesado albanés Kristian Prenga. Tyson Fury cuenta en el documental de Netflix, titulado 'Tyson Fury', que escuchaba voces en su cabeza que amenazaban con matarlo a él y a su familia. El boxeador, que protagoniza un sincero relato sobre su lucha para cuidar su salud mental, cuenta que temía ser internado a la fuerza mientras vivía en "lo más profundo del infierno", antes de que le diagnosticaran esquizofrenia. Su esposa Paris temió lo peor y reconoció que "tenía muchísimo miedo... Sentía mucho miedo por él". El documental se central en su época cuando, estando hundido de forma descontrolada en la depresión, el alcohol y las drogas, se enfrentó a Wladimir Klitschko para proclamarse campeón mundial en 2015. En junio de 2016 Tyson Fury fue trasladado de urgencia al hospital tras sospecharse que había sufrido un infarto. "Llego allí y Tyson me mira; tiene cables conectados por todas partes. Se le ve realmente aterrorizado. Me dice: 'Sácame de aquí. Los Illuminati, están todos metidos en esto. Como no pueden obligarme a guardar silencio, van a matarme"', recuerda su esposa Paris. Tyson Fury estaba sufriendo un ataque de ansiedad severo y experimentando delirios paranoicos: "La radio empieza a hablar, mantiene una conversación completa conmigo. Me dice: 'Nadie es intocable; podemos ir a por ti en cualquier momento. Si no te portas bien, mataremos a tu padre'. Me han drogado con ántrax... ¿acaso no estoy realmente aquí? Debo de estar muerto". "Fue entonces cuando vi a la psiquiatra. Me hizo un sinfín de preguntas. Cumplía con todos los requisitos: depresión, ansiedad, trastorno bipolar", recuerda el boxeador de 38 años. Paris confirmó que Tyson Fury "tiene una forma leve de esquizofrenia". "Ni siquiera entonces caí en la cuenta. Pensé: 'No digas tonterías, ¿de qué está hablando? Los esquizofrénicos son gente que ha perdido la cabeza. Pregunté: '¿Qué es el trastorno bipolar?'. Cuando me lo explicaron, pensé: 'Vaya, eso lo describe a la perfección'", recuerda la mujer de Fury. Tyson Fury mostró síntomas de su enfermedad desde su infancia, "recuerdo sentir ansiedad, a pesar de que no iba a ocurrir nada malo. Tenía cinco o seis años", pero no fueron detectados por su entorno. Su padre John cuenta que "no quería ver a un chico deprimido. Si lo vi, no le presté atención. Ahora entiendo que es una enfermedad terrible. Yo mismo la padezco". "Llevo la lucha en la sangre. Nunca seré otra cosa... En mi familia, mientras crecía, no había muestras de cariño ni cursilerías. Son todos tipos muy duros. No se expresan emociones. Como decía 50 Cent: 'No muestres afecto; el afecto puede costarte la vida'" recuerda el propio Tyson Fury.

articles.title: Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia and bipolar disorder diagnosis ahead of Anthony Joshua fight
articles.summary: Tyson Fury has opened up on being diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in a new feature-length Netflix documentary; Fury was diagnosed following his victory against Wladimir Klitschko in 2015; he is preparing to fight Anthony Joshua on December 11
articles.body:
Fury is set to end his long wait to fight Anthony Joshua on December 11, and ahead of the blockbuster British bout, a new feature-length Netflix documentary, TYSON FURY, will shed light on his career and his mental health struggles.

Fury defeated Wladimir Klitschko in November 2015, and was due to fight the Ukrainian again in October 2016, but withdrew after being declared "medically unfit to fight".

After his victory against Klitschko, the 'Gypsy King' revealed he had struggled with drug and alcohol addiction and had gained weight.

He was admitted to hospital in June 2016 with a suspected heart attack, and revealed that while in hospital he had heard voices in his head.

"Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury said during the Netflix documentary, which is due to air on November 27.

"It was like a living version of the pits of hell.

"I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.

"The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that's when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London. She asked me a gazillion questions, and I ticked all the boxes. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder."

During his stay in hospital, Fury explained he believed the "radio started talking to me" and voices had threatened to kill him and his family.

His wife Paris, whom he married in 2008, visited her husband in hospital and was told by doctors that the British fighter had suffered an anxiety attack.

"I was so scared, scared for him. I could see he was gone, he'd flipped the switch," Paris said.

Paris added: "[The doctors said] he's a mild schizophrenic and even then, the penny didn't drop.

"I was like: 'Don't be silly, what's she on about schizophrenic? Maniacs are schizophrenic, you're not schizophrenic'.

"I'd never heard of bipolar. When someone actually explained it to me, it was: 'Wow, that's him to a T'."

The NHS says Schizophrenia is a long-term mental health illness that is a form of psychosis.

Those suffering from the condition may, at times, be unable to distinguish their own thoughts from reality. Symptoms can include hallucinations and delusions.

The NHS describes bipolar disorder as a mental health issue where a person can experience extreme changes in their mood.

Fury, who has been open about his struggles with mental health in the past, spoke during the documentary about how he would go on to seek professional help for his condition.

He would return to professional boxing three years after his victory over Klitschko, before winning the WBC world heavyweight belt with a victory over Deontay Wilder in December 2018.

During the documentary, Fury credits his family for helping him through that period.

"If you look at my life, there's a lot of achievements, a lot of good stuff, a lot of success," he said.

"But the most successful thing I have in my life is my family, my kids and my wife."

If you've been affected by anything discussed in this article, support is available; please visit Sky Viewer Support .

If you are worried about your mental health, get advice and support through your GP or call the NHS on 111.

articles.title: Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis in new Netflix documentary
articles.summary: Tyson Fury describes hearing voices in his head when he suffered a breakdown in 2015, and was also diagnosed with bipolar disorder.
articles.body:
Tyson Fury says he was diagnosed with schizophrenia soon after his world title win over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

British heavyweight Fury, 38, says he heard voices in his head threatening to hurt him and his family.

In a documentary which will be released by Netflix on Friday, Fury and wife Paris describe how he was diagnosed after being admitted to hospital with a suspected heart attack in June 2016.

"Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury says.

"It was like a living version of the pits of hell. I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.

"The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that's when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London. She asked me a gazillion questions, and I ticked all the boxes. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder."

Doctors said Fury had suffered an anxiety attack.

Fury recalls hearing the radio talking to him, and begging Paris to get him out of the hospital because "the Illuminati" wanted him.

In the period after his victory over Klitschko, Fury gained weight and struggled with drug and alcohol addiction.

"It got that bad I was hearing voices in my mind," he says.

"I wouldn't be able to sit and have a conversation because I'd be hearing stuff in my mind.

"I didn't know where to turn and no-one knew what to do. I really needed help, or check into rehab or something.

"I never got a break from it for years. I wanted to be what I thought was normal again."

After Fury was released from hospital, a diagnosis of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder was confirmed.

The NHS describes schizophrenia , external as a form of psychosis, and symptoms can include hallucinations, delusions and muddled thoughts and speech. It says the main symptom of bipolar disorder , external is extreme changes to your mood.

Fury describes a "turning point" in 2017 when he was on a night out for Halloween.

"I went out and I was embarrassed by how I looked," he says.

"I was a fat mess and I had a glow-in-the-dark skeleton suit with full face mask on.

"I looked around and could see all the young people and I thought, 'I had the world in my hands and I threw it all away, and now I'm a fat mess addicted to alcohol'."

He says that was the beginning of a comeback which led him to focus more on his family and to return to training.

It resulted in another world title when he beat Deontay Wilder in 2020.

Fury is preparing for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight against Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on 11 December.

The fight will be broadcast live on Netflix.

articles.body: For Tyson Fury, the years following his 2015 victory over Wladimir Klitschko brought a collapse that few outside his inner circle fully understood. Behind the scenes, the heavyweight champion was battling severe mental health problems, hearing voices and becoming increasingly convinced that he and his family were in danger. Now, he has offered a deeply personal account of that period.‘Words can’t explain the darkness I was in’Fury, 38, says he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder after being admitted to hospital in June 2016 with a suspected heart attack. I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.“The anxiety was crippling me. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder.”Fury recalls hearing voices and believing that the radio was speaking directly to him. During his hospital admission, he begged his wife, Paris, to get him out because he believed the Illuminati wanted to kill him.Paris, 36, describes the moment she arrived at the hospital in the documentary. “I get there and Tyson looks at me, he’s got wires around him. He looks seriously frightened.”She recalls him telling her: “Get me out of here. The Illuminati, they’re all in on it. They can’t make me be quiet so they’re going to kill me.”Paris also told The Sun that she initially struggled to understand the diagnosis. “He’s a mild schizophrenic,” she says, before recalling her reaction when doctors explained the condition.“I thought ‘Don’t be silly, What’s she on about? Maniacs are schizophrenic.’”She added: “I asked ‘What’s bipolar?’ When someone explained it I thought, ‘Wow, that’s him to a tee’.”Fury says the problems had begun long before his hospital admission. “It wasn't new. I got to 25, 26 and thought I’m just struggling now. I’ve always been struggling my whole life.”He also recalls experiencing anxiety as a child, even when there was no apparent reason to feel frightened. “I remember having a feeling of anxiety even though nothing bad was going to happen. I was five or six.”Addiction, isolation and the Halloween turning pointThe period after Fury defeated Klitschko was marked by a sharp decline in his personal life. He struggled with alcohol and cocaine addiction, gained considerable weight and found it increasingly difficult to manage his thoughts.“It got that bad I was hearing voices in my mind,” he says.“I wouldn't be able to sit and have a conversation because I'd be hearing stuff in my mind.“I didn't know where to turn and no-one knew what to do. I need your help.’ And that was the comeback.”He returned to training and began rebuilding his life, with a greater focus on his family. The recovery eventually took him back to the top of heavyweight boxing, culminating in his victory over Deontay Wilder in 2020 and another world title.Fury has also spoken publicly about the need to manage mental health rather than expect it to disappear. In a 2019 interview with The Telegraph, he compared the experience to the Eagles song Hotel California.“In that song there is a verse that says, ‘You can check out anytime you want, but you can never leave.’ And that’s mental health.“You can check out and try and get better, but the mistake you make is trying to leave. Because it won’t never let you leave. You must learn to maintain the disease of mental health.”“It’s a silent killer,” he added.Fury prepares for Anthony Joshua showdownFury is now preparing for his long-awaited all-British heavyweight contest against Anthony Joshua, scheduled for December 11, 2026, at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.The fight, described as a £200 million contest, is being billed as one of the biggest heavyweight match-ups of the generation. Fury called it the “biggest of our time and of our generation” during a press conference in London.The bout will be broadcast live on Netflix, which is also releasing the documentary Tyson Fury on November 27. articles.title: Amber Moss-Birch: 21-year-old British amateur star signs with Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions
articles.summary: Gifted 21-year-old Amber Moss-Birch, a World Youth champion as an amateur, has signed with Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions; This is the first time MVP have signed a British amateur ahead of their pro debut
articles.body:
A brilliant amateur boxer, Moss-Birch became a World Youth champion in 2022. She's also won European gold and bronze medals at age group level among a host of accolades.

This is the first time MVP have signed a British amateur ahead of their pro debut.

Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, the founders of MVP, said: "The UK is the pound-for-pound champion of boxing talent and we are thrilled to sign our first British amateur, Amber Moss-Birch, one of the country's most exciting young amateur fighters.

"Amber has the determination and discipline to become a major force in the professional ranks. As we continue to expand and build the future of boxing, we're committed to giving exceptional young fighters like Amber the opportunities and platform to become global stars. We look forward to her professional debut in early 2027."

Moss-Birch's decorated amateur career includes gold at the 2019 European School Boxing Championships in Tbilisi, Georgia, and bronze at the 2022 European Youth Boxing Championships in Sofia, Bulgaria.

Later that year, she captured gold at the 2022 World Youth championships in La Nucia, Spain, delivering a dominant first-round stoppage of Uzbekistan's Oltinoy Sotimboeva in the 81kgs light-heavyweight final.

Throughout her amateur career, Moss-Birch amassed 14 international gold medals and four national championships.

Moss-Birch said: "I am absolutely over the moon signing with MVP. I have been watching what they have been doing for women's boxing, and this decision was a no-brainer. I sparred Chantelle Cameron for her last camp, and after speaking with her about MVP, I could not wait to make the move. I have signed a very good contract, and their plans for me are very exciting.

"I'm looking forward to making my debut in early 2027 and my partnership with Jake, Nakisa and the team."

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua undercard: Martin Bakole steps in for Jai Opetaia to fight former heavyweight world champion Deontay Wilder
articles.summary: Martin Bakole will replace Jai Opetaia and fight Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11; Bakole lost to Joseph Parker at short notice and has scored outstanding wins over Tony Yoka, Carlos Takam and Jared Anderson
articles.body:
Fury and Joshua finally meet after a long-running rivalry in the main event at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

Wilder is a former WBC heavyweight world champion renowned as one of the hardest punchers in the sport.

He was due to box Australian cruiserweight star Jai Opetaia, who withdrew injured and will now remain in the 200lb division.

Bakole was already scheduled to box on the card and is no stranger to taking a big fight on short notice. He travelled at just three days' notice to step in for Daniel Dubois and box Joseph Parker.

Prior to that Bakole scored outstanding wins over Tony Yoka, Carlos Takam and elite American hope Jared Anderson.

Opetaia's promoter Dana White said: "Jai Opetaia had to withdraw from his fight against Deontay Wilder next month. Stepping in is Martin Bakole, a six-foot-six, 300lb knockout artist who's ready to take on one of the hardest-hitting heavyweights in boxing.

"Wilder and Bakole have 66 wins and 59 knockouts, so you don't want to miss this fight."

Welsh heavyweight Moses Jolly also joins the card in a bout against Igor Adiel Macedo with more bouts still to be announced.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Deontay Wilder to fight Martin Bakole on undercard
articles.summary: Heavyweight Martin Bakole will face former world champion Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury's fight with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on 11 December.
articles.body:
Heavyweight Martin Bakole will face former world champion Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury's fight with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on 11 December.

The 33-year-old Congolese fighter replaces Australian Jai Opetaia, who withdrew after aggravating a hand injury in training.

Scotland-based Bakole had been scheduled to fight unbeaten Nigerian Solomon Adebayo on the bill, but will instead face 41-year-old Wilder in the co-main event.

Bakole suffered a second-round knockout defeat by Joseph Parker in February 2025 , having accepted the fight on just two days' notice.

He then fought to a majority draw with Nigerian Efe Ajagba in May 2025 and has not competed since.

Former WBC heavyweight champion Wilder, who has 43 knockouts in 45 victories, is looking to build on his split-decision win over Britain's Derek Chisora in April .

Unbeaten cruiserweight Opetaia, 31, was set to make his heavyweight debut against Wilder but pulled out of the contest last week.

Several British heavyweights, including Chisora, Richard Riakporhe, Frazer Clarke and Johnny Fisher had expressed an interest in facing Wilder following Opetaia's withdrawal.

Fury v Joshua - boxing's epic unfinished story

Who else is on the Fury-Joshua undercard?

Fury and Joshua's long-awaited showdown has been more than a decade in the making.

After years of failed negotiations, the fight was finally agreed with the financial backing of Saudi boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh and will be streamed globally on Netflix.

They are expected to contest the WBA 'super' heavyweight title at Cardiff's Principality Stadium, with ringwalks planned for no earlier than 01:00 GMT on Saturday, 12 December.

But despite the magnitude of the main event, the undercard has so far failed to match the anticipation surrounding one of the biggest fights in British boxing history.

Wilder remains a recognisable name among British fans, largely because of his memorable trilogy with Fury, but a contest against Bakole is unlikely to capture the imagination of the wider public.

Boxing records website BoxRec currently lists only Fury-Joshua on the event, although Netflix has announced further bouts in a social media post.

Welsh heavyweight Moses Jolly (12-0-1, 8 KOs) will face Brazil's Igor Macedo , who has won 15 of his 16 professional fights, with 14 victories by knockout.

Swansea-fighter Jolly, 30, is unbeaten and last fought in August, when he drew with Italian Guido Vianello at London's O2 Arena.

Unbeaten 21-year-old American prospect Da'Mazion Vanhouter (14-0, 11 KOs) will face Belgium's Michael Essomba (11-2, 10 KOs) in another heavyweight contest.

Boxing great Manny Pacquiao and Cardiff's former world champion Joe Cordina had both been linked with appearances on the undercard, although Pacquiao is no longer expected to feature.

It remains unclear whether any further bouts will be added to the event.

articles.title: Tyson Fury Opens Up About Schizophrenia Diagnosis and Mental Health in New Netflix Documentary
articles.summary: Before facing Anthony Joshua on Netflix next month, former heavyweight champion Tyson Fury will be the subject of an eye-opening documentary.
articles.body:
Before facing Anthony Joshua on Netflix next month, former heavyweight champion Tyson Fury will be the subject of an eye-opening documentary.

Per Deadline's Jesse Whittock , the 38-year-old revealed in the upcoming Tyson Fury documentary that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia shortly after his 2015 title win over Wladimir Klitschko. The documentary will debut on Netflix on Friday.

After his title win against Klitschko, Fury didn't fight again for three years. In the documentary, he will also discuss his bipolar diagnosis in 2017.

"Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury said about his mental health issues. "I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100% thought at times I'd end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.

"I was waking up in the night like this, the anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it. Completely gone, and that's when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London. She asked me like a gazillion questions, and I ticked all the boxes, whatever was going on. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder."

Fury went on to reveal the night he decided to turn his life around, on Halloween 2017.

"I went out and I was embarrassed of how I looked," he said. "I was a fat mess and I had this big costume on, a glow in the dark skeleton suit and I thought no one would recognize me in this. And I looked around me and I could see all like young people and I thought I've had the world in my hands and I threw it all away. And now, I'm just a fat mess, addicted to alcohol and, go home. I just said, 'I can't do this on my own anymore. I need your help.' And that was the part, the comeback."

The 90-minute doc also includes commentary from Fury's wife, Paris Fury, and father, John Fury.

"I can tell you this: When I look back, it's always been there," John Fury said. "Me being who I am and no understanding of anything, I didn't want to see a depressed kid – and if I did see it, I paid no mind to it. But I understand now. It's an illness, a terrible illness. I suffer with it myself."

After returning to boxing in 2018, Fury went unbeaten in his next 10 fights before losing the WBC heavyweight title to Oleksandr Usyk in 2024. He and Joshua, a fellow former heavyweight champion, will face off in a long-awaited showdown on Dec. 11 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, with the WBA (Super) heavyweight title up for grabs.

articles.title: MMA: James Gallagher retires from fighting aged 30
articles.summary: Northern Ireland fighter James Gallagher says circumstances outside his control have "forced" him to retire from MMA aged 30.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland fighter James Gallagher says circumstances outside his control have "forced" him to retire from mixed martial arts aged 30.

Gallagher has been a key figure in the Irish fighting landscape since bursting on to the scene as a teenager.

But after repeated injury setbacks and struggling for consistency in recent years, Gallagher has decided to hang up his gloves.

"This is not how I wanted my career to end. It is not a decision I made lightly, and it is certainly not a decision made because I lost the desire to fight," Gallagher posted on Instagram.

"The reality is, circumstances and stipulations outside of my control have forced me into a position where I can no longer continue doing what I have dedicated my entire life to.

"There are things happening behind the scenes that I cannot speak about at this moment.

"But there will come a time when I can tell my side of the story, and when that time comes, people will understand."

Gallagher came through John Kavanagh's SBG team ranks as a teenager, turning professional in 2015 a week before his 19th birthday.

His brash personality and grappling skills quickly drew attention to him as he stormed into a 7-0 perfect record with six submissions.

Repeated comparisons to Conor McGregor did not stop Gallagher from carving his own path and becoming one of Bellator's most recognisable stars.

Gallagher fought five times in Dublin, always drawing a big crowd, and his first defeat in 2018 came via knockout by Ricky Bandejas in the United States.

The Strabane native regrouped to win four in a row but was beaten by Patchy Mix in 2021 in front of a home crowd.

Mix went on to be Bellator champion while Gallagher's career stalled because of injuries and inactivity.

Gallagher was one of Bellator's key European stars but left soon after the MMA promotion merged with the Professional Fighters League (PFL) in 2024, and following a third defeat of his career by Leandro Higo.

He was wished a happy retirement by a host of Irish sport stars including Paul Hughes, Mick Conlan and McGregor.

Former UFC fighter Paddy Holohan branded Gallagher "a young veteran" of the fight game.

"From a young kid growing up in the Ireland, finding his place through martial arts, to signing with Bellator at 18, competing against some of the best in the world, reaching number six in the world, fighting at Madison Square Garden, selling out crowds at the 3Arena, and representing Ireland on the international stage, I gave this sport everything I had," Gallagher said.

"The sacrifices, the injuries, the weight cuts, the training camps, the missed moments with family, the highs, the lows, the setbacks, the comebacks.

"People see the walk to the cage, but they rarely see everything that goes into it."

Gallagher was marked as a future world champion from a young age, but despite not reaching that feat, he said he had "no regrets".

"I know what I have accomplished. I know what I sacrificed. And I know what I deserved.

"To my family, coaches, team-mates, sponsors, supporters, and everyone who stood by me throughout this journey - thank you. You helped make a kid's dream become a reality."

He would fight twice more in MMA, his most recent in Japanese promotion Rizin last April where he lost to Kazumasa Majima via submission.

Gallagher retires with an overall record of 13 wins and four losses.

articles.title: Don’t fence in Amir Albazi after UFC Qatar comeback submission
articles.summary: See if you can grab onto this: Amir Albazi rallied from a point deduction against Alessandro Costa to pull of a submission – and won a bonus for it.
articles.body:
Amir Albazi met the media Saturday after his win over Alessandro Costa at UFC Fight Night 294.

Albazi (18-3 MMA, 6-2 UFC) finished Costa (17-6 MMA, 5-4 UFC) with just 26 seconds left in their fight on the prelims at ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar. Albazi had a blatant fence grab and lost a point in the second, but it kept him alive in the fight so he ultimately could get the finish instead of going to the scorecards.

The fight was a rematch of one that took place nearly four years ago. In that one, Costa made his promotional debut and was knocked out in the third round of a fight he took on short notice when he stepped in as the third opponent for Albazi after Alex Perez and Brandon Royval both pulled out.

"It feels amazing. It's been a tough year for me. I had two losses. Coming back with a win means the world to me. I had a bunch of surgeries, a bunch of injuries, so this is just a story of adversity to come back in the win column. I always go in with that mentality – you have to kill me to get me out of there."

"First time, i knocked him out. Second time, I choked him out. I don't know what they want. Maybe next time, I'll just beat him up for a decision, instead."

articles.title: Dalton Smith: Paths align better for Shakur Stevenson unification than Adam Azim fight
articles.summary: Dalton Smith has had an outstanding 2026, winning and defending the WBC super-lightweight world title with wins over Subriel Matias and Alberto Puello; Smith believes he can headline at Hillsborough Stadium in his Sheffield hometown with American star Shakur Stevenson a potential opponent
articles.body:
Sheffield's Smith has had an outstanding year, knocking out Subriel Matias in New York to win his world championship and defending the belt against Alberto Puello in his Sheffield hometown.

American star Shakur Stevenson secured the WBO's super-lightweight championship when he beat Teofimo Lopez in January.

Both Smith and Stevenson are looking for their next opponents and a unification between the pair would be an appealing match up.

"Boxing's business and if it makes good business on both sides it's definitely a fight that can be made. Obviously there's other champions, other belts. I just want to be part of the biggest fights," Smith told Sky Sports .

"It's a fight where the paths align a little bit better than me and Adam Azim right now. But like I said we'll see."

His advice to Azim is: "Be in world level fights.

"It's a fight what gets talked about a lot," Smith said of Azim. "I've got my own path I'm going on. I'm not just saying I'm doing. I think Adam needs to play his part as well.

"I'm not really concentrating on Adam. I'll let him do what he's doing.

"I'm concentrating on a big 2027 for me."

He would love to headline at Hillsborough Stadium in Sheffield next year.

"I'm in a position now to be part of some big, big fights," Smith said. "I'd love to have Hillsborough, I'd love to win more world titles.

"It's something I've dreamt of for years, I've always said it. People probably thought I was delusional at the time saying it, but I kept following the dream and I feel like it's very close. Possibly something we can get over the line next year. It'll just be big for Sheffield, big for the city and I'll be proud to say I've done it.

"I feel like I'm carrying that torch for the city now."

articles.title: Imane Khelif still set for professional contest in Paris on December 15 despite withdrawal of original opponent
articles.summary: Imane Khelif was the subject of a fierce gender eligibility row at the Olympic Games; she hasn't boxed since winning gold at Paris 2024; Algerian is due to fight as a professional in Paris on December 15
articles.body:
Algeria's Khelif won Olympic welterweight gold in Paris in 2024, while a fierce gender eligibility row overshadowed her participation.

Khelif was cleared to compete by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), despite the International Boxing Association (an organisation that itself has been banned from Olympic boxing) having banned her from the previous year's World Championships for allegedly failing to meet gender eligibility criteria.

Khelif hasn't boxed since beating Liu Yang in that Olympic final, but is due to have a professional bout in Paris on December 15.

That fight next month will go ahead although Khelif's original opponent Clarida Sarabia has withdrawn and Khelif is now looking for a replacement.

"The opponent did have to withdraw from the fight for administrative reasons," a spokesperson ⁠for promoter Stair Event ​told Reuters.

"But the bout ​is still scheduled for December ​15. We'll announce the opponent ⁠soon."

In February, Khelif said she was open to genetic testing ⁠only if administered by ​the IOC.

articles.title: American tourist killed in fight with MMA fighter known as ‘Frank the Tank’ in Bangkok hotel lobby over noise complaint
articles.summary: A fatal altercation between an American tourist and an Italian ex-MMA fighter over a noise complaint at a Bangkok hotel resulted in death. The incident raises questions of self-defense amid ongoing investigations.
articles.body: A noise complaint at a Bangkok hotel reportedly turned deadly after an American tourist became involved in a physical altercation with an Italian former MMA fighter. The confrontation, captured on security cameras, ended with the tourist losing consciousness and later dying. The former fighter was arrested on suspicion of murder but maintains that he acted in self-defence.Hotel confrontation turns fatal after argument over noiseThe incident happened on Sunday morning at Tim Place Hotel in Bangkok, Thailand, involving Harper, 46, from Michigan, and Marques, 39, an Italian Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt and former MMA fighter known as “Frank the Tank”.According to police and security footage cited by the New York Post, Harper had gone downstairs to complain about noise coming from another floor. During the exchange, he allegedly threatened to cut the throat of the hotel's receptionist, Khang On Nan Kham Bway, 32.The receptionist told Viral Press, as quoted by the New York Post, that she had suggested Harper move to the fifth floor if he found the noise excessive.“I told him that if he thought it was too loud, he could move to the fifth floor. We hadn’t even finished talking when the Italian man walked in,” she said.Marques, who was reportedly a regular guest at the hotel, then walked towards the elevator. According to Khang, he passed Harper without touching or brushing against him, but the American followed him towards the lifts and began exchanging words with him.“The Italian walked past calmly without touching or brushing against the American,” Khang said.“The American followed him into the lift area. They started exchanging words, but I couldn’t understand exactly what they were saying because they were speaking English.”The receptionist also alleged that Harper had previously threatened her during an earlier noise complaint.“The American had threatened me once before, saying that if it was still noisy upstairs, he would cut my throat,” she said.Khang described Marques as a mild-mannered regular guest, while saying Harper was a recent arrival whose behaviour had made her feel “unsafe”.Security footage shows fight inside elevator areaThe sequence of events was captured by the hotel's security cameras. According to footage described by the New York Post, Marques entered the elevator while Harper continued speaking to him from the lobby.The 5ft 8in, 140-pound former fighter reportedly leaned out from the elevator doors and asked, “You talking to me?” Harper then suggested that they “step outside”.Marques appeared to move back into the elevator, but Harper forced the closing doors open and pulled him out into the lobby. The American then placed the Italian in a headlock, according to the footage.Khang said Harper forced the elevator doors open with such force that they broke.“As the lift doors were closing, the American forced them open so violently that they broke. Then they started fighting,” she said.The confrontation continued in front of the receptionist, who reportedly tried unsuccessfully to intervene. Marques eventually turned the situation around, overpowering Harper and pinning him to the floor. Harper's body appeared to go limp during the struggle.Attempts to revive him with CPR outside the hotel were reportedly unsuccessful.‘Frank the Tank’ arrested as police investigate self-defence claimPolice from Khlong Tan station were called to the hotel at around 8.40am local time. Officers found Harper dead, with an abrasion on his forehead, while Marques remained at the scene and waited for investigators.According to The Pattaya News, Marques was taken into custody on suspicion of murder after police pronounced Harper dead. He reportedly maintained that he had acted in self-defence.The security footage appears to show Harper initiating the physical confrontation, but police are continuing to examine the circumstances surrounding the death. Authorities have also indicated that Marques's martial arts experience will form part of their investigation.“The suspect has fighting skills and is believed to be involved in MMA. He appears to be an experienced fighter,” Police Captain Sirichai Kaewprasit told Asia Pacific Press.Marques is an Italian Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt and former professional MMA fighter. His record is listed as 2-1 by Tapology.Despite the apparent sequence captured on camera, prosecutors are pursuing a charge of intentional homicide, with officials citing Marques's fighting background as part of the case. The suspect has not been convicted, and the question of whether he acted in self-defence remains subject to the investigation and legal proceedings.Police are reviewing witness statements, security recordings and forensic evidence. Harper's body has been sent for a post-mortem examination, while investigators are coordinating with the US Embassy in Bangkok to notify his family.The investigation is ongoing, with authorities yet to establish their final account of the circumstances that led to the American tourist's death.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Makhachev, sobre el ataque de los Nurmagomedov a Merab: "En Daguestán hay peleas todos los días"
articles.standfirst: El campeón de peso wélter de la UFC ha salido en defensa de sus amigos y ha justificado la agresión a Dvalishvili y su amigo Saba Lazishvili
articles.summary: El campeón de peso wélter de la UFC ha salido en defensa de sus amigos y ha justificado la agresión a Dvalishvili y su amigo Saba Lazishvili
articles.body: Hace poco más de una semana, Usman Nurmagomedov, Umar Nurmagomedov y varios acompañantes atacaron brutalmente a Merab Dvalishvili y su amigo Saba Lazishvili antes de un evento de RAF en Abu Dhabi. Esto provocó su detención y que fuesen condenados a una multa económica y a seis meses en prisión, aunque Khabib intervino y logró sacarles de la cárcel. Además, recientemente Islam Makhachev ha justificado la agresión y ha defendido a sus amigos y compañeros de entrenamiento. La rivalidad entre Umar Nurmagomedov y Merab Dvalishvili se remonta a enero de 2025, cuando se vieron las caras y acabaron en malos términos. Sin embargo, todo escaló en un RAF Georgia de este año cuando Merab dio un tortazo a un miembro del 'Clan Nurmagomedov' e insultó a su madre, algo sagrado en su cultura. A pesar de que Dvalishvili pidió perdón y parecía que estaban en buenos términos, Usman y Umar se tomaron la justicia por su mano y les asaltaron por sorpresa junto a varios compañeros para darles una brutal paliza. La situación escaló rápidamente y tras salir a la luz los vídeos ambas partes implicadas fueron detenidas. Dvalishvili y Saba fueron liberados a las 48 horas y compitieron en RAF con victoria para ambos, pidiendo la libertad de sus agresores a pesar de todo lo que había sucedido. Pocos días después, Khabib viajó a Abu Dhabi y negoció con las autoridades para lograr la libertad de sus primos, y ahora ha sido Islam Makhachev el que ha justificado todo lo sucedido. "Todo se sacó totalmente de quicio. En Daguestán, tenemos peleas todos los días. En Georgia, Merab se comportó de manera vergonzosa: insultó a la madre de alguien. Por lo que sé, esa persona perdió a su madre. Para mí, eso es algo sagrado. No creo que los nuestros hayan hecho nada malo. Uno tiene que hacerse responsable de sus palabras. Si cruzas la línea, debes atenerte a las consecuencias. Cuando se insulta tu honor, no importa si es uno contra uno o dos contra uno", respondió en unas declaraciones recogidas por 'a_futbole'. De hecho, en ningún momento el 'Clan Nurmagomedov' ha pedido disculpas por lo sucedido, por lo que se entiende que no están arrepentidos. Al contrario, ya que se han justificado por sus actos y no han parado de repetir que fue Merab el que comenzó todo al faltar el respeto a la madre de uno de los suyos. Merab, por su parte, ya se disculpó por la parte que le toca después de recibir la agresión, pidió su libertad y afirmó haber perdido todo el respeto que tenía por Usman y Umar Nurmagomedov. De hecho, Umar no estaba en un principio en el ataque, pero diversas fuentes apuntan a que llegó cuando la situación se había calmado y volvió a agredir a Merab hasta que la situación empeoró aún más. Por si fuera poco, todo esto ha ocurrido en medio de los rumores del fichaje de Usman Nurmagomedov por la UFC ahora que es agente libre. Eso sí, Dana White ha sido preguntado al respecto y no le ha dado demasiada importancia, por lo que lo normal es que la incorporación del primo de Khabib al peso ligero de la promotora se anuncie en los próximos meses para conocer quién será su primer rival.

articles.title: Ruby White wins flyweight gold at European Under 23 Championships while two British team-mates also collected medals
articles.summary: Ruby White impresses at the European Under 23 Championships; The teenager won gold at flyweight, handing Ukraine's Taisiia Pokusai two counts in the final round as she secured another significant international medal; GB's Oliver Male secured a bronze while Ella Thompstone took silver
articles.body:
The teenager from Sturminster Newton has excelled at youth level and stepped up to senior boxing to secure a silver medal at the Commonwealth Games earlier this year.

She has now added another significant medal to her collection beating Ukraine's Taisiia Pokusai in the 51kgs final.

White edged ahead after the opening round, landing a right to the head of her taller opponent. Pokusai was tricky, moving well to box from range.

But White built up her work, threading a one-two through a Pokusai attack and hitting her stride in the third and final round. White stepped in with a firm jab and sent the Ukrainian to the canvas with a left hook.

She lashed in further punches to give Pokusai a second count, making sure of victory in the gold medal match.

"I'm over the moon, big respect to my opponent. I boxed last year in the Europeans and she's improved so much and it's nice to face her in the ring again. All my respect, let's go! Five-time European champion!" the 19-year-old White said afterwards.

Other GB boxers won medals, with Oliver Male securing bronze at 80kgs while Ella Thompstone took silver at 65kgs.

articles.title: Carlos Prates isn't buying into UFC 336's interim championship: 'Not a real title'
articles.summary: Even one-half of UFC 336's controversial co-main event doesn't view the interim title as legitimate.
articles.body:
Carlos Prates is determined to try to make 2027 a year filled with gold.

The Fighting Nerds superstar became an instant fan favorite when he arrived in the UFC through Dana White's Contender Series in November 2023. Eight fights later, Prates has been a consistent entertainer and provider of highlight-reel knockouts. His path now leads to his biggest opportunity yet: An interim welterweight title tilt against undefeated contender Michael Morales at UFC 336 on Jan. 30.

Prates, 33, said on Tuesday's edition of "The Ariel Helwani Show" that he'll receive the same payout for UFC 336 that he would if the fight was for Islam Makhachev's undisputed welterweight title. That, however, doesn't mean Prates is treating it the same.

"I'm happy, but I'm not thinking about money. Of course the money is good, but if you do things the right way, the money's going to come anyway," Prates told Uncrowned.

"I think about the title. I want to get the title. An interim title, for me, is not the real title. Not the real champ. That's the point. Of course I want the belt, that's part of the prize. I work hard for this, and if I fight for the interim title, it's not my fault. It's Islam's fault because he said he wants to fight and be active, blah, blah, blah. Now he's running.

"But, for sure, it's not a real title. I don't feel like it is."

The interim title fight drew plenty of questions when it was first announced , after the sport's pound-for-pound king successfully defended his UFC title in August with a decision win over Ian Machado Garry. UFC CEO Dana White said that Makhachev chose not to fight, opting to instead wait until Ramadan passes in March 2027.

There was never an official offer on the table for an undisputed title tilt, says Prates, but he was admittedly frustrated to see the verbally agreed matchup fall apart.

"Everybody agreed to fight in January, and Islam said, 'Yeah, of course, let's fight. I want to be active,'" Prates said.

"A month and a half [later], the UFC called me and said, 'Islam is out of the fight.' They didn't say why. He just said he didn't want to fight in January."

In recent bouts, Prates has made it a point to become the first fighter to knock out opponents who never have been KO'd before. Makhachev's lone career loss came in a knockout back at the start of his UFC run in October 2015, so that's off the table. Instead, Prates promises to retire the former lightweight champ after he gets through Morales.

"I'm going to make him retire from MMA," Prates said of Makhachev.

"I promise you, when I meet him inside the Octagon, I'm going to hit him so hard he's going to think, 'Oh my God, I'm never going to fight again.'"

Although Prates vs. Morales arguably shouldn't be happening next, given Makhachev's health and the fact that either contender has a strong case for a title shot, it's still as good of a fight as the UFC can make right now. Morales has been less active than Prates, going all of 2026 without a fight. Nonetheless, Prates still views Morales as a worthy opponent in an interim bout.

If it were Morales against Makhachev, though? Not so much.

"I don't think [he's at the level of the top guys]," Prates said of Morales. "Maybe striking [is his weakness]. He's strong. He comes forward and throws some punches, but when he gets somebody who's a really good striker, who knows how to move, how to defend, it's going to be hard.

"Probably he's a good wrestler because he's strong, he's big. Let's see the cardio also. I don't think the fight is going to be five rounds. I can fight five, seven, eight rounds, but I don't know about him because he's got a lot of weight."

articles.title: Nelson Hysa aims to beat Agit Kabayel, win WBC world title and take on Tyson Fury, his 'favourite fighter'
articles.summary: Nelson Hysa challenges Agit Kabayel for the WBC title on Saturday in Dusseldorf; Hard-punching Hysa hopes to upset popular German Kabayel and then look to take on his 'favourite fighter' Tyson Fury; Hysa says Moses Itauma is still the best in the division - 'I don't want to fight him!'
articles.body:
Hysa, unbeaten in 25 professional fights, challenges Kabayel on Saturday for the WBC heavyweight world championship.

The Albanian has taken 23 of those wins inside the distance and is looking to upset the popular German when they fight in Dusseldorf this weekend.

A power-puncher, Hysa told Sky Sports : "The knockout was with me from the first day that I started boxing.

"In this match [against Kabayel] I am preparing to do more good rounds because I know the opponent is a very good boxer, he's a tough boxer, a serious boxer.

"But we are planning, we are trying to do our best. We have our strategy to win the match and I think we will win the match earlier than the 12th round.

"I need to move up the ratio of knockouts!"

With Oleksandr Usyk vacating his championships, there are now new belt-holders in the division, but Hysa does not consider Kabayel the best of the current heavyweight titlists.

"For me No 1 now of the guys that have the belts, No 1 is Filip Hrgovic, [then Daniel] Dubois and for me the special one is Tyson Fury.

"Hrgovic will do very good because he's a good boxer," Hysa added. "Hrgovic beat the best guy in the heavyweight division. He beat Moses [Itauma]. I don't want to do a fight with Moses, he's a good guy! He will be the best heavyweight in the world. He is the best heavyweight in the world but he needs more time."

Fury will fight Anthony Joshua for the WBA 'super' heavyweight title when they meet on December 11. Hysa tips Fury to win and is eager to box him in a unification if he comes through his own fight.

"Who doesn't want to fight Tyson Fury? He's a legend," Hysa said. "The No 1 man at heavyweight.

"He's my No 1 favourite boxer, I love him, I love everything he does. His style, everything.
